summary: After the July 2012 revolution, peace committees were set up at the residential street level in addition to neighborhoods and villages, enabling localities with prior experience to deliver justice without chaos.

citation.chapter: 9. The New Justice System Consensus Is Key
citation.quote: And after July 2012, they were set up at the residential street level as well. Those cities and villages that had had experience with peace committees experienced no chaos or confusion in delivering justice and became the go-to places for settling civil and criminal cases.

title: July 2012 liberation opens new possibilities for Rojava's education movement
summary: The July 2012 liberation of Rojava created new possibilities for the education movement. The MGRK's bodies decided to train many hundreds of teachers to meet growing demand.

citation.quote: The July 2012 liberation, explained Berîvan, "provided us with a new situation, with previously unimaginable possibilities."

title: Liberation of Rojava and establishment of post-revolutionary council governance
summary: Following the liberation of July 2012, the councils took on the task of ensuring economic stability and basic provisions. Their prior existence of at least a year gave them a critical advantage in managing the transition.

citation.quote: After the liberation of July 2012, the councils had the task of ensuring that the economy didn't collapse and that basic provisions remained available.

title: Economics commissions impose price caps on markets and businesses
summary: On the second day of the revolution, economics commissions set price caps on markets and businesses to prevent speculators from hoarding food and medications. The controls ensured uniform prices for food and diesel.

citation.quote: On the second day of the revolution, the economics commissions set price caps on the markets and on businesses, to prevent speculators from hoarding food and medications in order to profit when prices later rose.

title: Hewlêr Agreement signed, establishing the Supreme Kurdish Council
summary: The MGRK and ENKS reached the Hewlêr Agreement under Barzanî's mediation, establishing the Supreme Kurdish Council (SKC) with five members from each bloc to serve as the highest authority in Rojava.

citation.quote: On July 11, mediated by their host, Barzanî, the blocs came to an agreement. This Hewlêr Agreement stipulated that the two groups would share power during a transitional phase, and to this end it established the Supreme Kurdish Council (SKC).

title: Hewlêr Agreement signed and Supreme Kurdish Council (SKC) founded
summary: The MGRK and ENKS concluded the Hewlêr Agreement, creating the Supreme Kurdish Council (SKC) to ensure unity among Kurds shortly before the liberation of Rojava began.

citation.chapter: 6.5 The Supreme Kurdish Council (SKC)—Desteya Bilind a Kurd
citation.quote: Shortly before the liberation began, on July 11, 2012, the MGRK and the ENKS concluded the Hewlêr Agreement [see [4.4]] and created the Supreme Kurdish Council (SKC), to ensure unity among Kurds.

title: Syrian opposition forces launch offensive on Damascus and Aleppo
summary: Armed Syrian opposition forces launched an offensive on Damascus and Aleppo on July 18, 2012, prompting the MGRK and YPG to anticipate an imminent FSA incursion into Rojava.

citation.chapter: 6.2 The People’s Council of West Kurdistan (MGRK)—Meclîsa Gela Rojavayê Kurdistan
citation.quote: On July 18, 2012, armed Syrian opposition forces launched an offensive on Damascus and Aleppo. The MGRK and YPG expected that the FSA and others would enter Rojava soon, to attack the state there.

title: Kobanî city first in Rojava to expel the Ba'ath regime
summary: On July 19, 2012, Kobanî city became the first city in Rojava to expel the Ba'ath regime, marking a pivotal moment in the Rojava revolution.

citation.quote: On July 19, 2012, Kobanî city was the first in Rojava to expel the Ba'ath regime.

title: YPG and MGRK supporters liberate Kobanî from Assad's regime
summary: At 1 a.m. on the night of July 18–19, 2012, YPG fighters secured the roads around Kobanî while the population occupied state institutions. Regime soldiers, surrounded by the mass of people, surrendered without bloodshed and were released.

citation.quote: At 1 a.m. on the night of July 18–19, 2012, the YPG took control of the roads leading in and out of Kobanî city. Inside the city, the majority of the people, who supported the MGRK, occupied the state institutions.

title: Rojava revolution begins in Kobanî
summary: On July 19, 2012, the revolution started in Kobanî, marking the moment Rojava's new direct-democratic social order—organized over the preceding year since March 2011—came into effect.

citation.chapter: 6.2 The People’s Council of West Kurdistan (MGRK)—Meclîsa Gela Rojavayê Kurdistan
citation.quote: The next day, the revolution started in Kobanî. In just over a year, from March 2011 to July 19, 2012, Rojava had established its new direct-democratic social order.

title: July 19 revolution in Rojava
summary: Eight days after the Hewlêr Agreement, the MGRK and YPG carried out the July 19 revolution liberating Rojava's cities, in which the ENKS played no role.

citation.chapter: 6.5 The Supreme Kurdish Council (SKC)—Desteya Bilind a Kurd
citation.quote: Eight days later the MGRK and YPG carried out the July 19 revolution, in which the ENKS played no role.

title: Liberation of Rojava begins; justice commissions established
summary: Following the liberation that began on July 19, 2012, TEV-DEM instigated the creation of justice commissions in each district. These commissions took charge of liberated courts and prisons, freed political prisoners, and began building a new justice system.

citation.quote: After the liberation that began on July 19, 2012, justice commissions (in Kurdish, dîwana adalet) were established for each district at the instigation of the TEV-DEM.

title: Mass demonstration and battle in Şêx Maqsûd; 13 civilians killed
summary: During Ramadan, more than 3,000 people demonstrated demanding the FSA withdraw from Şêx Maqsûd. The FSA responded by firing on residents from buildings; the YPG fought back and 13 civilians and several FSA fighters were killed in the hours-long battle.

citation.quote: During Ramadan, on August 19, more than 3,000 people demonstrated in support of this demand. But the FSA didn't withdraw—instead, it fired at the residents from buildings. The YPG fought back, and in the hours-long battle, 13 civilians and several FSA fighters were killed.

title: Kurdish-language instruction begins in most Rojava schools
summary: In September 2012, Kurdish-language instruction began in most schools, especially in Afrîn and Kobanî and in the Kurdish neighborhoods of Aleppo.

citation.quote: In September 2012, Kurdish-language instruction did indeed begin in most schools, especially in Afrîn and Kobanî, and in the Kurdish neighborhoods of Aleppo.

title: Addendum to Hewlêr Agreement institutes joint Kurdish military leadership
summary: Kurdish parties agreed on an addendum to the Hewlêr Agreement in November 2012, instituting a joint Kurdish military leadership, though disagreements over a second military force quickly emerged.

citation.chapter: 6.5 The Supreme Kurdish Council (SKC)—Desteya Bilind a Kurd
citation.quote: In November 2012 the parties agreed on an addendum to Hewlêr, instituting a joint Kurdish military leadership.

title: Al-Nusra and Ghuraba al-Sham invade Serêkaniyê
summary: Up to 3,000 heavily armed Al-Nusra and Ghuraba al-Sham fighters crossed the Turkish border and entered Serêkaniyê, where only 39 YPG fighters were present. After four days of fighting, jihadist and FSA units occupied the city.

citation.quote: In November 2012, up to 3,000 heavily armed Al-Nusra and Ghuraba al-Sham units crossed the Turkish border and entered Serêkaniyê. Hardly any YPG units were in the city, only 39 YPG fighters, and they were cut off from supplies.

title: National Coalition of Syrian Revolutions and Opposition Forces created
summary: The SNC participated in forming the National Coalition of Syrian Revolutions and Opposition Forces, hosted by Qatar, to strengthen US, NATO, and Gulf State influence in Syria, furthering the Islamization of opposition forces.

citation.chapter: 14.1 The Islamization of the Syrian Opposition
citation.quote: In November 2012, the SNC participated in the creation of the National Coalition of Syrian Revolutions and Opposition Forces (NC), which was formed in order to strengthen the influence of the United States, NATO, and the Gulf States in Syria.

title: Jihadist attack on Serêkaniyê
summary: Around 3,000 heavily armed jihadists from Al-Nusra and parts of the FSA crossed the Turkish-Syrian border at Ceylanpınar and attacked Serêkaniyê. After four days of fighting they occupied the city, imposing massacres, devastation, and Sharia law for seven months.

citation.quote: In November 2012, about 3,000 heavily armed jihadists—Al-Nusra and parts of the FSA, like the Syrian Islamic Liberation Front (SILF)—slipped over the Turkish-Syrian border at Ceylanpınar and attacked Serêkaniyê.

title: Al-Nusra attacks YPG checkpoint and murders council co-chair Abid Xelîl
summary: Al-Nusra attacked a YPG control point and burned a flag of the Supreme Kurdish Council. When Abid Xelîl, co-chair of the people's council, arrived for scheduled peace talks, jihadists murdered him.

citation.quote: A few days after the invasion, on November 18, Al-Nusra attacked a YPG control point, and some of its supporters burned a flag of the Supreme Kurdish Council. Talks were to be held, but when Abid Xelîl, the co-chair of the people's council, showed up for the meeting, the jihadists murdered him.

title: Supreme Military Council founded in Antakya
summary: The Supreme Military Council (SMC) was established in Antakya, Turkey, as a new command structure for the Syrian opposition forces. Salafist and jihadist groups such as the Syrian Islamic Liberation Front quickly gained dominance within it.

citation.chapter: 14.1 The Islamization of the Syrian Opposition
citation.quote: In Antakya, Turkey, in December 2012, the Supreme Military Council (SMC) was founded as a new command structure for the mainly nondemocratic opposition forces.

title: IS attempts to capture Kobanî canton
summary: In late 2013, the Islamic State attempted to capture Kobanî canton and city, but the YPG and YPJ repeatedly repulsed its attacks.

citation.quote: In late 2013, IS attempted to capture the canton and the city, but the YPG and YPJ repeatedly repulsed its attack.

title: Kurdish movement accepts responsibility and apologizes for Hamidiye militia's role in genocide
summary: The Kurdish movement in North Kurdistan formally accepted historical responsibility and apologized for the Kurdish Hamidiye militia's collaboration with the Ottoman genocide, becoming the only force within Turkey to do so.

citation.quote: In 2013, the Kurdish movement in North Kurdistan accepted historical responsibility and apologized for the Kurdish Hamidiye militia's collaboration with the genocide. It is the only force within Turkey to have done so.

title: Publication of Democratic Autonomy of Women by Dengê Jiyan
summary: The women's movement published "Malbata Demokratik û hevratiya azad" (The Democratic Family and the Free Life Together) in the volume Xweseriyademokratik a jin (Democratic Autonomy of Women), issued by Dengê Jiyan in 2013.

citation.quote: "Malbata Demokratik û hevratiya azad" [The Democratic Family and the Free Life Together], in Xweseriyademokratik a jin [Democratic Autonomy of Women] (Dengê Jiyan, 2013).

title: 135 women participate in Kobanî women's council
summary: In the spring of 2013, 135 women participated in the Kobanî women's council to address local women's issues. The council was created by a women's house (mala jinan) in Kobanî so women could make decisions autonomously.

citation.quote: In the spring of 2013, 135 women participated in the Kobanî women's council to address local women's issues.

title: Kurdish Women's Press Association (RAJIN) founded in Qandil Mountains
summary: The Kurdish Women's Press Association (RAJIN) was founded in the Qandil Mountains in 2013, establishing an organized union for Kurdish women journalists.

citation.quote: The Kurdish Women's Press Association (RAJIN) was founded in the Qandil Mountains in 2013.

title: IS abducts, rapes, and murders Armenian women in Hesekê province
summary: According to Asya Abdullah, IS forces abducted, raped, and murdered a large number of Armenian women in Hesekê province in the summer of 2013, targeting the region's multi-ethnic peaceful coexistence.

citation.quote: According to Asya Abdullah, in the summer of 2013 in Hesekê province, IS "abducted, raped, and murdered a large number of Armenian women."

title: MGRK launches campaign to spread communes to rural areas
summary: After communes proved to be a positive development in urban areas, the MGRK initiated a broad campaign in 2013 to extend the commune system to rural areas of Rojava.

citation.chapter: 6.2 The People’s Council of West Kurdistan (MGRK)—Meclîsa Gela Rojavayê Kurdistan
citation.quote: In 2013, after the communes proved to be a very positive development, the MGRK would initiate a broad campaign to spread them to rural areas.

title: IS and Al-Nusra Front attacks restrict MGRK movement between cantons
summary: In the summer of 2013, attacks by IS, Al-Nusra Front, and other Islamist organizations made it difficult for MGRK activists to travel between Rojava's three cantons.

citation.quote: In the summer of 2013, attacks by IS, Al-Nusra Front, and other Islamist organizations made it difficult for MGRK activists to move among the three cantons.

title: YPG defends Aleppo against Islamic and armed opposition groups
summary: In the summer and fall of 2013, the YPG successfully defended Aleppo, pushing back attacks by Islamic and other armed opposition groups as well as parts of the FSA.

citation.quote: In the summer and fall of 2013, the YPG defended Aleppo well, pushing back attacks by Islamic and other armed opposition groups, as well as parts of the FSA.

title: Islamic State begins entering Aleppo
summary: At the end of 2013, the Islamic State (IS) started to enter the city of Aleppo, adding a new armed actor to the already complex conflict.

citation.quote: But at the end of 2013, IS started to enter the city of Aleppo.

title: IS, Al-Nusra, and FSA mount massive attacks on Rojava's three cantons
summary: After the summer of 2013, Islamic State, Al-Nusra, and parts of the Free Syrian Army launched massive attacks on Rojava's three cantons while the ENKS and Iraqi KDP remained silent and blocked aid from entering.

citation.chapter: 6.5 The Supreme Kurdish Council (SKC)—Desteya Bilind a Kurd
citation.quote: Relations deteriorated after the summer of 2013, mainly because while IS, Al-Nusra, and parts of the FSA mounted massive attacks on Rojava's three cantons, the ENKS and the Iraqi KDP remained uncannily silent and did not even permit aid to enter Rojava.

title: Rojava councils succeed in refining petroleum into diesel at scale
summary: By summer 2013 the Rojava councils had organized petroleum refining in sufficient quantities to produce diesel locally, preventing another catastrophic winter deforestation campaign.

citation.chapter: Attack on the Qamişlo City Hall
citation.quote: By the summer of 2013, the councils finally succeeded in refining petroleum in greater quantities into diesel, thereby avoiding another total wipeout of trees the following winter.

title: Three ENKS parties defect to join Rojava's transitional administration
summary: In late 2013 and early 2014, three leftist Kurdish parties—the PÇKS, the Kurdish Leftist Party, and the PDK-S—announced they would leave the ENKS coalition and join the transitional administration, but were preemptively expelled by the ENKS before they could do so.
people: Democratic Leftist Party of Kurds in Syria

citation.quote: In late 2013 and early 2014, three leftist parties—the Democratic Leftist Party of Kurds in Syria (Partiya Çepa Kurdî li Surîyê, PÇKS), the Kurdish Leftist Party, and the Democratic Kurdish Party of Syria (PDK-S)—decided to leave the ENKS and announced that they would join the transitional administration.

title: Autonomous women's military units created within YPG
summary: In early 2013, autonomous women's units were created within the defense forces, recognizing women fighters as essential to both Rojava's defense and women's liberation.

citation.quote: Since women fighters were considered essential both to the defense of Rojava and to the struggle for women's liberation, autonomous women's units were created in early 2013.

title: Law academy established in Qamişlo
summary: The law academy in Qamişlo was established in 2013 with the primary objective of training people for Rojava's new justice system. It also scrutinizes existing Syrian laws and supports the work of the justice parliaments.

citation.quote: The law academy in Qamişlo follows the discussions from a neutral distance. Established in 2013, the academy's first objective is to train people for the justice system.

title: AZDW teacher-training academy founded in Qamişlo
summary: In the fall of 2013, the AZDW was founded in Qamişlo to systematically train teachers and develop a new education system. Similar academies were also created in Afrîn and Kobanî.

citation.quote: In the fall of 2013, the AZDW was founded in Qamişlo to systematically train teachers and develop the intended new education system.

title: Arab-majority schools request Kurdish-language instruction
summary: After the winter of 2013–14, several schools with mainly Arab students asked for Kurdish-language instruction, showing Democratic Autonomy gaining ground among non-Kurdish groups.

citation.quote: But after the winter of 2013–14, several schools with mainly Arab students asked for it.

title: Kurdish listed as course on student certificates in liberated regions
summary: In the summer of 2013, Kurdish was listed as a course on many students' certificates in the liberated regions, forcing the Syrian state to accept Kurdish-language instruction.

citation.quote: But finally in the summer of 2013, in the liberated regions, Kurdish was listed as a course on many students' certificates.

title: Afrîn schools selected as pilot project for Kurdish-language instruction
summary: In the fall of 2013, some schools in Afrîn canton were chosen as a pilot project to teach primary classes in Kurdish, beginning Rojava's stepwise shift away from Arabic-medium schooling.

citation.chapter: 10.3 The Academy for Kurdish Language, History, and Literature (AZDW)
citation.quote: In the fall of 2013, some schools in Afrîn were selected as a pilot project. Two years later, most primary schools in Afrîn decided to teach mostly in Kurdish.

title: Small hospitals established for war wounded in Rojava
summary: In 2013, hospitals and clinics in Rojava proved unable to adequately care for all the war wounded, leading to the establishment of small dedicated hospitals for this purpose.

citation.quote: In 2013, hospitals and clinics proved unable to adequately care for all the war wounded, so small hospitals were established for this purpose.

title: Protests in North Kurdistan demand medication access to Rojava
summary: People in Nisêbîn and Mêrdîn took to the streets demanding the Turkish government allow medications and supplies to cross the border into Rojava, ultimately forcing a government concession.

citation.quote: In 2013, people in Nisêbîn and Mêrdîn, in North Kurdistan, took to the streets and demanded that the Turkish government permit medications and supplies to be transported across the border into Rojava. They ultimately forced the government to concede, as Ayşe Gökkan, the former mayor of Nisêbîn, told us.

title: Legal importation of medical supplies into Rojava begins
summary: Following successful protests, starting in spring 2013 medical supplies and medications could legally be imported into Rojava via the Turkish border, passing through Turkish Red Crescent controls.

citation.quote: Starting that spring, supplies and medications could legally be imported. They have to pass through controls by the Turkish Red Crescent, after which local authorities in North Kurdistan transport them across the border, where health assembly staff receive them.

title: Grain mills constructed in Rojava to avert famine
summary: To address the critical flour shortage of the previous winter, several grain mills were constructed in 2013, securing the food supply across Rojava's cantons.

citation.quote: To avert a famine, several grain mills were constructed in 2013.

title: Kobanî achieves adequate supply of baked goods
summary: By the end of 2013, Kobanî's wheat production had risen sufficiently to provide an adequate supply of baked goods to the canton.

citation.quote: Kobanî's wheat production rose, so that by the end of 2013 it had an adequate supply of baked goods.

title: Diesel refining from crude oil begins in Cizîrê
summary: In the summer of 2013, the refining of crude oil into diesel started in Cizîrê, helping to stabilize the canton's economy and making fuel more affordable under council-controlled price caps.

citation.quote: As for oil, the refining of crude into diesel started in the summer of 2013, which helped stabilize Cizîrê economically.

title: Building boom across all three Rojava cantons
summary: In 2013 and 2014, all three cantons of Rojava experienced a building boom, driven in part by an influx of refugees from other parts of Syria requiring housing.

citation.quote: In 2013 and 2014, all three cantons saw a building boom.

title: Two-story construction height limit lifted near Turkish border
summary: In autumn 2013, the regime-era restriction capping building height at two stories within 25 kilometers of the Turkish border was lifted, and residents were permitted to build up to four stories.

citation.quote: But in the autumn of 2013, the two-story cap was lifted, and people were allowed to build up to four stories.

title: First cooperatives established in Rojava
summary: The first cooperatives were launched in Rojava in 2013, marking the beginning of the region's social economy project under Democratic Autonomy.

citation.quote: The first cooperatives were rolled out in 2013.

title: YPG captures 587 jihadists; only 91 of Syrian origin
summary: According to the YPG, of 587 jihadists captured in 2013, only 91 were of Syrian origin, illustrating the overwhelmingly foreign composition of IS forces.

citation.quote: According to the YPG, of the 587 jihadists who were captured in 2013, only 91 were of Syrian origin.

title: Syrian Women's Initiative founded
summary: The Syrian Women's Initiative was founded in 2013, comprising Kurdish, Arab, and Syriac women as a potential partner for the Rojava self-government.

citation.quote: Another possible partner is the Syrian Women's Initiative, founded in 2013 and comprising Kurdish, Arab, and Syriac women, but it will not be easy for this initiative to gain a foothold outside Rojava.

title: Jabhat Al-Nusra and FSA occupy Serêkaniyê
summary: From January until July 2013, Islamist forces of Jabhat Al-Nusra together with FSA units occupied the city of Serêkaniyê in Cizîrê Canton.

citation.quote: From January until July 2013, Islamists of Jabhat Al-Nusra as well as FSA units occupied Serêkaniyê.

title: Sakine Cansız, Fidan Doğan, and Leyla Şaylemez murdered in Paris
summary: In January 2013, Kurdish activists Sakine Cansız, Fidan Doğan, and Leyla Şaylemez were murdered in Paris. Tens of thousands of people in Aleppo's Kurdish neighborhoods demonstrated in their memory, risking bombardment by the state.

citation.quote: In January 2013, when Sakine Cansız, Fidan Doğan, and Leyla Şaylemez were murdered in Paris, they demonstrated in the tens of thousands, risking bombardment by the state to do so.

title: Syriac Military Council founded in Rojava
summary: The Syriac Military Council (Mawtbo Fulhoyo Suryoyo, or MFS) was founded and immediately joined forces with the YPG to fight IS, operating mainly in areas where Syriacs live in Hesekê province.

citation.quote: And on January 8, 2013, the Syriac Military Council (Mawtbo Fulhoyo Suryoyo, or MFS) was founded. It operates mainly in areas where Syriacs live, especially in Hesekê province. The day it was formed, the MFS joined forces with the YPG to fight IS.

title: Sakine Cansız and two other Kurdish women's activists murdered in Paris
summary: Sakine Cansız, Fidan Doğan, and Leyla Şaylemez — three women's movement activists — were murdered in Paris.

citation.chapter: 3.1 The PKK and its Paradigm Shift
citation.quote: On January 10, 2013, she and two other women's movement activists, Fidan Doğan and Leyla Şaylemez, were murdered in Paris.

title: Human Rights Watch report on press freedom in Iraqi Kurdistan
summary: A Human Rights Watch report documented severe limitations on press freedom in the KRG, highlighting the security apparatus used to maintain the KDP-PUK patronage system.

citation.quote: it has repeatedly used violence and repression against protesters, accompanied, according to a 2013 Human Rights Watch report, by severe limitations on press freedom.

title: Jihadists overrun Til Koçer region
summary: In March 2013, jihadists overran the Til Koçer region, prompting most Arab residents to flee to nearby Kurdish villages where they were welcomed, with about ninety tribal representatives requesting YPG assistance.

citation.quote: In March 2013, when jihadists overran the Til Koçer region, most of the Arab residents fled to the nearby Kurdish villages, where they were graciously accepted.

title: Newroz 2013 celebrated under siege as attacks escalate
summary: At Newroz 2013, the situation in Aleppo's Kurdish neighborhoods was described as excruciating. Though the Kurds held the two strategic upland neighborhoods, both the state and the FSA intensified pressure and tightened the embargo in response to Kurdish neutrality.

citation.quote: But at Newroz 2013, the situation was excruciating. The Kurds controlled those two strategic upland neighborhoods, but the councils resisted being used by either one side or the other. The Kurds' neutrality angered both sides, the state and the FSA, which escalated their attacks.

title: Jabhat Al-Nusra seizes Til Koçer and surrounding villages
summary: Islamists of Jabhat Al-Nusra overran the town of Til Koçer (Al Yarubiya) and its border crossing, expelling the predominantly Arab population and massacring those who refused to leave.

citation.quote: At the other end of Cizîrê canton, in March 2013, Islamists of Jabhat Al-Nusra overran Til Koçer (in Arabic, Al Yarubiya) and the surrounding villages. They occupied the town, with its border crossing, and drove out the local population, which was predominantly Arab.

title: FSA military head calls Al-Nusra "our partners"
summary: Abdul Jabbar Akidi, military head of the FSA from Aleppo and responsible for FSA operations in northern Syria, stated that Al-Nusra fighters are "partners" and not terrorists, defending their shared goal of ousting Assad.

citation.quote: Abdul Jabbar Akidi—military head of the FSA from Aleppo and militarily responsible for the FSA in northern Syria and head of the Lîwa al-Tawhid (which is aligned with the Muslim Brotherhood and supported by Qatar)—was asked about Al-Nusra on March 29, 2013. "They are our partners," he said.

title: Aleppo people's council orders mass evacuation to Afrîn and Rojava
summary: In April 2013, the Aleppo people's council decided to evacuate most of the population to Afrîn and other parts of Rojava for safety. Approximately 400,000 people — some 75–80 percent of the population — were evacuated, with most of those remaining being young people.

citation.quote: In April 2013, the Aleppo people's council decided to evacuate most of the population to Afrîn and other parts of Rojava for safety, while it continued to try to hold on to northern Aleppo. The evacuation was poorly planned—people rushed out into the roadways. But some 400,000 were safely evacuated, some 75–80 percent of the population.

title: YPJ (Women's Protection Units) founded
summary: The YPJ was formally founded on April 4, 2013, in parallel to the YPG, with all women previously in YPG mixed units automatically becoming members.

citation.quote: The YPJ was founded on April 4, 2013, in parallel to the YPG. All women who were previously in the YPG's mixed units automatically became members.

title: First YPJ fighter killed in defense of Afrîn city
summary: The first YPJ fighter, Meryem Mihemed (Şehîd Şîlan), fell in the defense of Afrîn city in May, shortly after the YPJ was founded in April 2013.

citation.quote: In May, the first YPJ fighter fell in the defense of Afrîn city: Meryem Mihemed (Şehîd Şîlan), who had been born there in 1991.

title: YPG offensive liberates Serêkaniyê from Al-Nusra
summary: After months of alternating ceasefires and intense clashes, the YPG mounted an offensive in June 2013 and drove Al-Nusra from Serêkaniyê, liberating holy places and protecting civilians of all ethnicities.

citation.quote: After five cycles of ceasefire and open warfare, the YPG finally became strong enough that in June 2013 it mounted an offensive.

title: YPG/YPJ liberates Serêkaniyê from jihadist occupation
summary: The YPG/YPJ expelled Al-Nusra and the FSA from Serêkaniyê, ending a seven-month jihadist occupation that had been marked by massacres and the imposition of Sharia law.

citation.quote: In June 2013, as we have seen, the YPG/YPJ liberated Serêkaniyê and expelled Al-Nusra and the FSA.

title: Al-Nusra Front and Al-Qaeda attack Rojava, triggering Syriac exodus
summary: When the Al-Nusra Front and Al-Qaeda in Syria attacked Rojava in July 2013, Syriac Christians in Hesekê province and Serêkaniyê faced kidnappings and murders of businesspeople, nuns, bishops, and prominent figures, prompting a mass exodus to Turkey and Europe.

citation.quote: In July 2013, when the Al-Nusra Front and Al-Qaeda in Syria were attacking Rojava, Syriacs were living in the southern part of Hesekê province and in Serêkaniyê. Businesspeople, nuns, bishops, and well-known personalities were kidnapped and murdered, which resulted in a mass exodus to Turkey and Europe.

title: Egyptian president Mohamed Morsi ousted in military coup
summary: Mohamed Morsi was removed from the Egyptian presidency in a military coup in July 2013, weakening the Muslim Brotherhood's position across the Middle East including its influence in Syria's FSA and National Council.

citation.quote: But in July 2013, Morsi was ousted in a military coup, which weakened the general position of the Muslim Brotherhood in the Middle East.

title: Al-Nusra and ISIS begin attacks on Rojava from Dêrîk to Afrîn
summary: Beginning July 16, 2013, Rojava forces were attacked by Al-Nusra, ISIS, and other Islamist groups across a wide front from Dêrîk to Afrîn, with the Turkish army also attacking and killing YPG members.

citation.quote: "But since July 16, 2013, we have been attacked by Al-Nusra and ISIS and other Islamist groups, from Dêrîk to Afrîn. And the Turkish army attacked us. Turkish sharpshooters killed two of our friends. They openly supported the Islamists and attacked us directly."

title: US Congress approves weapons deliveries to the FSA
summary: The US Congress approved weapons deliveries to the Free Syrian Army, a decision that came shortly before FSA commanders openly threatened to exterminate the Kurdish population of Rojava.

citation.quote: On July 23, 2013, the US Congress approved weapons deliveries to the FSA.

title: FSA commanders meet in Antep and issue communiqué against Rojava
summary: Seventy FSA commanders met with SMC leadership in Antep, Turkey, and issued a communiqué threatening the Kurdish people of Rojava. Commander Abdul Jabbar Akidi vowed to 'yank them out by the roots.'

citation.quote: On July 26, seventy FSA commanders met with SMC leadership in Antep (Dîlok), in Turkey, and issued a communiqué against Rojava.

title: Massacre of Kurds at Til Hasil and Til Aran
summary: FSA and Al-Nusra forces, joined by the Kurdish Azadî Brigade, committed a massacre in the two Kurdish towns of Til Hasil and Til Aran near Aleppo. Approximately seventy people were killed, hundreds captured, and women were tortured and raped.
location: Til Hasil and Til Aran, Aleppo region, Syria

citation.quote: Over the course of July 31 and August 1, 2013, members of the FSA and Al-Nusra, together with the Kurdish Azadî Brigade (which adheres to the Azadî Party in the Kurdish National Council or ENKS), committed a massacre in Til Hasil and Til Aran, two towns near Aleppo that were not under the control of the Rojava self-government.

title: Jabhat Al-Akrad battles ISIS and is expelled from FSA
summary: After battling ISIS in August 2013, Jabhat Al-Akrad was excluded from the Free Syrian Army because of its presumed ties to the PYD.

citation.quote: Al-Akrad was founded as part of the FSA, but after battling ISIS in August 2013, it was excluded from the FSA because of its presumed ties to the PYD.

title: Movement between Cizîrê and Kobanî cantons cut off
summary: In August 2013, the route between Cizîrê and Kobanî cantons was severed by Islamist forces, isolating the cantons from one another.

citation.quote: In August, movement between Cizîrê and Kobanî was cut off, while movement between Kobanî and Afrîn remained possible until June 2014.

title: ISIS begins march through Syria, overruns Raqqa
summary: ISIS launched its advance through Syria in August 2013, capturing the city of Raqqa as part of its triumphal march through the region.

citation.quote: In August 2013, ISIS (the Islamic State in Iraq and the Levant) began its triumphal march through Syria, overrunning the city of Raqqa.

title: Asya Abdullah interview published in Radikal on women's freedom and democracy
summary: PYD co-chair Asya Abdullah gave an interview to Pinar Öğünç published in the Turkish newspaper Radikal, discussing the necessity of women's freedom for democracy in Rojava.

citation.quote: Asya Abdullah, interview by Pinar Öğünç, "Ohne die Freiheit der Frau keine Demokratie," *Radikal*, August 22, 2013, http://bit.ly/1QovIQD.

title: South Kurdistan parliamentary elections break KDP-PUK duopoly
summary: New parliamentary elections in South Kurdistan in September 2013 saw the Gorran Party win the second most votes, ending 19 years of KDP-PUK duopoly rule.

citation.chapter: Prologue: On the Road to Til Koçer
citation.quote: The KDP and PUK duopoly had been in power for 19 years in September 2013 when new parliamentary elections were held and the new Gorran Party gained the second most votes, thereby breaking the duopoly.

title: MGRK calls for common autonomous administration for all of Rojava
summary: The MGRK called for a common autonomous administration covering all three cantons of Rojava, even before it had exhausted internal discussions about its own problems and contradictions.

citation.quote: The first thing to note is that when the MGRK called for a common autonomous administration for all of Rojava in September 2013, it had not exhausted the discussions about its own problems and contradictions.

title: Aramaic-language instruction introduced in Dêrîk district schools
summary: In September 2013, Syriac communities in the Dêrîk district established a language and education institute and private schools offering instruction in Aramaic.

citation.quote: This started in September 2013, in the Dêrîk district, where the local Syriacs established a language and education institute and private schools giving instruction in their native tongue.

title: Zübeyde Sarı publishes "Women of Rojava" in Özgür Gündem
summary: Journalist Zübeyde Sarı published an article titled "Women of Rojava" in the Kurdish newspaper Özgür Gündem, documenting the central role of women in the Rojava revolution.

citation.quote: Zübeyde Sarı, "Women of Rojava," Özgür Gündem, September 8, 2013.

title: German government denies knowledge of jihadist massacres in Syria
summary: When asked in parliament about the jihadist massacres at Til Hasil and Til Aran, the German government responded that 'no substantial information is available on the question,' while claiming to seek information from KDP sources.

citation.quote: On September 9, 2013, when the German government was asked about the jihadist massacres in Syria in general and in Til Hasil and Til Aran in particular, its response was: "No substantial information is available on the question."

title: CARE publishes report on women's role after Arab Spring uprisings
summary: Care Deutschland-Luxemburg published a report finding that political groups that came to power after the Arab Spring in Egypt, Morocco, Yemen, and Palestinian areas surpassed their predecessors in conservatism and patriarchalism, worsening conditions for women.

citation.quote: Care Deutschland-Luxemburg E.V., Arabischer Frühling oder arabischer Herbst für Frauen? CARE-Bericht zur Rolle von Frauen nach den Aufständen im Mittleren Osten und Nordafrika, September 12, 2013.

title: YPG liberates Til Koçer
summary: In October 2013, the YPG liberated Til Koçer, winning the hearts of Arab and Christian residents who subsequently joined the YPG and YPJ in large numbers.

citation.quote: The following October, the YPG liberated Til Koçer, which won the hearts of the Arab and Christian residents, who proceeded to join the YPG in large numbers and even YPJ.

title: Rojava social contract presented to the public for comment
summary: A social contract sketched out by TEV-DEM and the MGRK was presented to the public in October 2013 for a three-month comment period, drawing in more than fifty organizations of Kurds, Arabs, Syriacs, and others.

citation.quote: A social contract was sketched out, which in October 2013 was presented to the public for comment. A dynamic unfolded such as the region had never before seen. The discussions went on for three months, and suggestions were collected.

title: YPG/YPJ liberates Til Koçer from Islamist control
summary: After ten days of fighting, YPG and YPJ forces drove out Jabhat Al-Nusra from Til Koçer in late October 2013, capturing abandoned tanks, artillery, and other war materiel left by the retreating jihadists.

citation.quote: The liberation took ten days, but in late October 2013, Til Koçer came under YPG/YPJ control. The terrorists fled, abandoning tanks, cars, heavy artillery, and other war materiel.

title: Warşîn sewing cooperative begins operations in Qamişlo
summary: The Warşîn sewing cooperative in Qamişlo started with two sewing machines and four workers, later growing to 40 machines and 25 workers producing clothing for Cizîrê canton.

citation.quote: The factory got under way in October 2013, with two sewing machines and four workers. Now the 40 machines and 25 workers produce clothing for Cizîrê canton.

title: Dr. Kurdaxi outlines Rojava's alternative economic model in ANF News
summary: An interview with Dr. Dara Kurdaxi, member of the economics commission in Afrîn, was published in ANF News on November 28, 2013, in which he argued that Rojava must reject capitalism and state socialism in favor of a different economic model.

citation.quote: "Ekonomist Kurdaxi: Suriye karanlığa, Rojava aydinlığa gidiyor," *ANF News*, November 28, 2013, http://bit.ly/1PeVwOp. All quotes from Dr. Kurdaxi in this chapter come from this source.

title: IS overruns Mosul
summary: Shortly after the authors' return from their May 2014 visit to Rojava, the Islamic State seized control of Mosul.

citation.chapter: Prologue: On the Road to Til Koçer
citation.quote: Only a week after our return journey, Mosul would be overrun by IS.

title: Islamist attack on Tirbespî
summary: Islamist fighters attacked a house in Tirbespî approximately two months before the authors' May 2014 visit, killing a YPG comrade; the YPG repelled them.

citation.chapter: Prologue: On the Road to Til Koçer
citation.quote: Two months earlier the Islamists attacked it, explains our companion Cûdî, martyring a heval. But the YPG fended them off, so they are now trying suicide bombs.

title: IS attacks Ezidis of Şengal
summary: In the summer of 2014, the Islamic State launched an attack against the Ezidi community in Şengal (Sinjar), triggering urgent calls for international assistance given IS's exterminationist policies.

citation.quote: In summer 2014, the Ezidis of Şengal were attacked by IS.

title: Battles for Şengal and Kobanî spotlight women's role in Rojava
summary: In the latter half of 2014, the battles for Şengal and Kobanî drew global attention to the prominent role of women in Rojava's society and armed resistance, transforming the image of Kurdish women in the West.

citation.quote: In the latter half of 2014, the battles for Şengal [see [8.9]] and Kobanî [see [14.2]] shined a spotlight on something the West had thought impossible: a Middle Eastern society with women at its center.

title: IS attack on Kobanî destroys gains of the revolution
summary: The 2014–15 attack by the Islamic State destroyed much that had been built in Kobanî, including the structures of Democratic Autonomy and women's organizing that had developed since the revolution.

citation.quote: The 2014–15 attack by IS destroyed much that was built in Kobanî.

title: KJK (Komalên Jinên Kurdistan) founded
summary: The KJK was founded in 2014 as the successor to the KJB (Supreme Women's Council), serving as the umbrella organization for all women's organizations supporting Democratic Confederalism and women's liberation ideology.

citation.quote: The KJK was founded in 2014 as the successor organization of the KJB (Koma Jinên Bilind, or Supreme Women's Council).

title: MGRK achieves support of more than 70 percent of Rojava's population
summary: By 2014, the MGRK system had gained the support of more than 70 percent of Rojava's population as well as seven Kurdish political parties.

citation.quote: By 2014, the MGRK system had achieved support of more than 70 percent of the population of Rojava. It also gained the support of seven Kurdish parties.

title: YPG concludes ceasefire with FSA and armed opposition groups in Aleppo
summary: In spring 2014, the YPG concluded a ceasefire with the FSA and other armed opposition groups. Al-Nusra also adhered to the ceasefire, enabling food and provisions to be supplied to non-regime areas via the Azaz border crossing.

citation.quote: In the spring of 2014, the YPG concluded a ceasefire with the FSA and other armed opposition groups. Al-Nusra, still present in the region, adhered to the ceasefire. As a result of the new circumstances, the areas that were not under regime control (Aleppo, Azaz, Idlib) could be supplied with food and other basic provisions over the border crossing at Azaz.

title: New city parks opened in Qamişlo, including Helepçe Xêlil memorial park
summary: In 2014 the Qamişlo councils opened new city parks planted with trees, including a memorial park in the Korniş neighborhood honoring Helepçe Xêlil, who had been killed in the April 2014 IS attack on the city hall.

citation.chapter: Attack on the Qamişlo City Hall
citation.quote: In fact, in 2014, some new city parks were laid out, and planted with trees. We visited a small park in the Qamişlo neighborhood of Korniş, which was opened as a memorial to Helepçe Xêlil, who had been murdered in a bomb attack on the Qamişlo City Hall in April 2014.

title: Pothole repairs on Rojava city streets and main roads
summary: In 2014, municipal workers filled potholes on city streets and main roads in Rojava cantons with asphalt, demonstrating the people's municipalities' capacity to maintain infrastructure under embargo.

citation.quote: In 2014, quite a few potholes in the city streets and on the main roads were filled in with asphalt. In 2015, many more roads in and around the cities of Cizîrê were blacktopped.

title: Geneva II conference organized to address Syrian conflict
summary: The United Nations, United States, and Russia organized the international "Geneva II" conference for late January 2014. The MGRK sought for months to secure Kurdish participation but was denied.

citation.quote: In the beginning of 2014, the United Nations, the United States, and Russia were organizing an international conference, known as "Geneva II," to be held at the end of January. For months, the MGRK had sought to ensure that the Kurds would be able to participate, but none of the powers were interested.

title: Culture and Art academy founded in Serêkaniyê
summary: The Culture and Art academy in Serêkaniyê was established in early 2014, quickly attracting 170 members including Arabs and Chechens, with facilities for theater, media, and literature.

citation.quote: The Culture and Art academy in Serêkaniyê was founded in early 2014 and had 170 members as of May, including numerous Arabs and Chechens.

title: IS militias approach Şengal as Peshmerga withdraw and disarm Ezidis
summary: Islamic State militias advanced on Şengal in northern Iraq, home to 350,000 Ezidis. Despite KDP promises of protection, Peshmerga forces withdrew without warning, disarmed the Ezidis, and the KDP failed to evacuate them.

citation.quote: In the summer of 2014, IS terrorist militias were approaching the city of Şengal, in northern Iraq, preparing to attack the 350,000 Ezidis who lived there.

title: People's courts in Rojava face intensive criticism
summary: Beginning in fall 2014, the people's courts came under intensive criticism for resembling hierarchical justice systems, with a small group making decisions rather than broad social participation.

citation.quote: Starting in the fall of 2014, the people's courts came under intensive criticism. According to the critics, they were beginning to resemble the courts in existing hierarchical justice systems.

title: IS attack and occupation destroys nearly finished Kobanî hospital
summary: The Islamic State's 2014 attack on and occupation of Kobanî destroyed the city's hospital facility, which had been almost finished. A new hospital was subsequently put under construction.

citation.quote: In Kobanî, the 2014 IS attack and occupation destroyed the facility there, which was almost finished, but now a new hospital is under construction.

title: Qamişlo military hospital established
summary: The Qamişlo military hospital was established in 2014, with capacity to treat up to 26 patients.

citation.quote: The Qamişlo military hospital, established in 2014, treats up to 26 patients.

title: Hospitals constructed in Afrîn and Kobanî
summary: Similar military hospitals were constructed in Afrîn and Kobanî during 2014–15, expanding health care infrastructure in those cantons.

citation.quote: Similar hospitals were constructed in Afrîn and Kobanî in 2014–15.

title: Health seminars introduced into Rojava schools
summary: Starting in 2014, the health assemblies introduced health seminars into schools in Rojava, expanding public health education.

citation.quote: Since 2014, health seminars have been introduced into the schools as well.

title: International volunteers begin supporting educational seminars in Rojava
summary: Since the fall of 2014, international volunteers have been supporting regular educational seminars in Rojava, contributing to the health assembly's public education efforts.

citation.quote: Since the fall of 2014, international volunteers have been supporting regular educational seminars in Rojava.

title: DAAs establish health ministries in Rojava
summary: The Democratic Autonomous Administrations created health ministries in 2014, incorporating the existing health assemblies and councils into them while retaining their autonomous and self-determining structure.

citation.quote: In 2014, the DAAs created health ministries. The health assemblies and councils became part of them.

title: Afrîn wheat harvest exceeds expectations and flour price reduced
summary: In 2014, the wheat harvest in Afrîn was greater than expected and two flour mills had been built from local materials, allowing the price of flour to be lowered to 3,500 Syrian pounds per bag.

citation.quote: In 2014, the wheat harvest was greater than expected, and two flour mills had been built from local materials, so the price of flour could be lowered to 3,500 pounds.

title: Cizîrê exports flour to the Kurdistan Regional Government
summary: By 2014, Cizîrê canton had achieved sufficient flour production to export to the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG), marking a significant economic milestone.

citation.quote: In 2014, Cizîrê was even able to export flour to the KRG.

title: Afrîn partially converts to wheat production
summary: In 2014, Afrîn canton partially converted its agricultural output to wheat production, improving the canton's self-sufficiency in food.

citation.quote: Afrîn partially converted to wheat production in 2014.

title: FSA and Jabhat Al-Akrad expel IS from Azaz
summary: In early 2014, the Free Syrian Army and Jabhat Al-Akrad expelled the Islamic State from Azaz, allowing Afrîn canton to better provide for itself economically.

citation.quote: In early 2014, the FSA and Jabhat Al-Akrad expelled IS from Azaz, allowing Afrîn to better provide for itself.

title: Dozdar Hemo describes Rojava's communal social economy to authors
summary: Cizîrê's economics adviser Dozdar Hemo told the authors in 2014 that Rojava was building a communal, social economy where everyone would have the opportunity to participate and achieve subsistence.

citation.quote: "We are building a communal, social economy," Dozdar Hemo, Cizîrê's economics adviser, told us in 2014. "Everyone should have the opportunity to participate and, as a minimal first step, to achieve subsistence."

title: Authors consult Qamişlo municipal officials on water crisis
summary: In 2014, the authors spoke with Qamişlo municipal officials who were aware of the water pollution crisis but cited limited financial and technical means as barriers to cleaning up the rivers.

citation.quote: When we spoke to Qamişlo municipal officials in 2014, they seemed highly aware of the problem, but because of limited financial and technical means, the possibilities for cleaning up the river are few.

title: Rojava establishes functioning waste collection services across all cantons
summary: By 2014, every location in Rojava had functioning services for trash collection and disposal, using repurposed pickup trucks, light trucks, and backhoes as garbage vehicles.

citation.quote: By 2014, everyplace in Rojava had functioning services for trash collection and disposal.

title: IS invades Şengal; KDP withdraws Peshmerga; YPG/YPJ/PKK rescue Ezidis
summary: When IS invaded Şengal to destroy the Ezidis, the KDP withdrew its 11,000 Peshmerga, leaving the Ezidi population nearly defenseless. The YPG, YPJ, and PKK intervened to rescue tens of thousands of Ezidis.

citation.quote: In the summer of 2014, as we have seen, when IS invaded Şengal to destroy the Ezidis, the Peshmerga failed to live up to their responsibility to protect them. In fact, the KDP withdrew its 11,000 Peshmerga and left the Ezidi population nearly defenseless, which could have led to a massacre of 10,000 Ezidis. But the YPG, the YPJ, and the PKK rescued tens of thousands of Ezidis from Şengal.

title: Turkish PM Davutoğlu describes IS fighters as driven by anger, not terrorists
summary: In 2014, Turkish Prime Minister Ahmet Davutoğlu publicly stated that IS jihadists were not terrorists but merely "young men driven by anger," reflecting Turkey's reluctance to oppose Islamic State.

citation.quote: In 2014, Prime Minister Ahmet Davutoğlu said that IS jihadists were not terrorists but merely "young men driven by anger."

title: Ilham Ahmed describes external power struggle over Syria
summary: Ilham Ahmed, summarizing Rojava's geopolitical situation, described Syria as an arena of competing international powers, each seeking to install its own system and retain influence in the Middle East.

citation.quote: "Every powerful country has its own plans for Syria," Ilham Ahmed summarized for us in 2014.

title: Emergency appeals for medical and humanitarian aid for Rojava launched
summary: Starting in autumn 2014, emergency appeals went out to Europe seeking medical and humanitarian donations for Rojava, with solidarity campaigns targeting women's institutions and cooperatives, and collections for weapons to preserve YPG/YPJ independence.

citation.quote: Since the autumn of 2014, emergency appeals have gone out to Europe, especially for medical and humanitarian aid, asking for donations.

title: Three cantons of Rojava declare Democratic Autonomy
summary: The three cantons of Rojava—Cizîre, Kobanî, and Afrîn—issued a declaration of Democratic Autonomy and created democratic-autonomous administrations for an inclusive, pluralistic system.

citation.quote: In January 2014, the three cantons of Rojava—Cizîre, Kobanî and Afrîn—went on to issue a declaration of Democratic Autonomy and thereby created "democratic-autonomous administrations" to ensure that their new system would be inclusive and pluralistic.

title: YPG's biggest military defeat at Til Hemîs
summary: In January 2014, the YPG suffered its biggest military defeat at Til Hemîs, where jihadists had overrun the town and some of the local tribe supported them, resulting in dozens of fighters killed.

citation.quote: This led to the YPG's biggest military defeat, in January 2014, when dozens of fighters lost their lives.

title: European Syriac Union endorses Democratic Autonomy in Rojava
summary: David Vergili of the Brussels-based European Syriac Union declared in January 2014 that Democratic Autonomy in Rojava recognizes the equal status of the region's peoples, and that the Syriacs are fighting to secure their rights in a reconstructed Syria.

citation.quote: David Vergili, member of the Brussels-based European Syriac Union, said in January 2014 that "Democratic Autonomy in Rojava recognizes the commonalities and equal status of the peoples of the region and represents them democratically and equitably."

title: Armed opposition groups drive Islamic State out of Aleppo and Azaz
summary: In January 2014, armed opposition groups advanced against the Islamic State and expelled it from Aleppo and Azaz.

citation.quote: In January 2014, armed opposition groups advanced against IS and drove it out of Aleppo and Azaz.

title: Social Contract approved in Rojava
summary: The Social Contract was approved in January 2014, prompting extensive discussion about the relationship between the MGRK council system and the newly formed Democratic Autonomous Administrations.

citation.quote: After the Social Contract was approved in January 2014, the relationship between the MGRK and the new DAAs was much discussed.

title: Democratic Autonomous Administrations (DAAs) founded in Rojava
summary: The three DAAs were formally founded in January 2014, after which the MGRK continued to function alongside the new administrative bodies, with MGRK activists running ministry projects.

citation.quote: After the DAAs were founded in January 2014, the MGRK continued to function regardless of the existence and functioning of the ministries.

title: IS takes control of Manbij
summary: The Manbij area along the Turkish border between the cantons of Afrîn and Kobanî/Cizîrê fell under IS control in January 2014.

citation.quote: The area, also known as Manbij, had been in the hands of IS since January 2014.

title: Justice ministries of Rojava's cantons founded
summary: The justice ministries of Rojava's three cantons were founded in January 2014, providing three representatives each to the justice parliaments while limiting their legal influence compared to conventional justice systems.

citation.quote: Each of the three cantons has one, and they consist of 23 people: three representatives from the justice ministries, founded in January 2014; eleven from the justice commissions, seven from the constitutional court, and two from the bar association.

title: Car bomb detonates in front of Kongreya Star office in Dêrîk
summary: A car bomb detonated in the center of Dêrîk in front of the Kongreya Star office, killing a father and child and spreading panic in the city.

citation.quote: In January 2014, a car bomb detonated in the center of Dêrîk, in front of the Kongreya Star office. A father and child were killed, and panic spread in the city.

title: Geneva II conference convened on Syrian civil war
summary: The Geneva II conference in January 2014 sought to bring together the Syrian National Coalition, Islamist-jihadist opposition, and the Syrian government to negotiate a solution to the civil war. Rojava's transitional government sought to participate but was blocked by Turkey's insistence that Kurds join "the opposition."

citation.quote: A similar conditionality was observable in the negotiations over participation at the Geneva II conference in January 2014 and Geneva III in January 2016.

title: Rojava's three cantons announce the Social Contract
summary: The three cantons of Rojava announced the Social Contract in January 2014, declaring themselves part of a democratic Syria and eschewing independence as a goal.

citation.quote: In January 2014, the three cantons announced the Social Contract, which says they regard themselves as part of a democratic Syria; the same is true of the Federal System of Rojava/Northern Syria, declared in March 2016.

title: Truck carrying grenades for Al-Nusra intercepted in Antep
summary: A truck was stopped in Antep on January 19, 2014, and found to be transporting grenades for Turkish intelligence (MİT) to the border town of Reyhanlı, where the driver admitted they were to be handed over to Al-Nusra.

citation.quote: On January 19, 2014, in Antep, a truck was stopped and found to be transporting grenades for the MİT (Turkish intelligence) into the border town of Reyhanlı. The truck driver admitted that once there, he was to hand over the weapons to Al-Nusra.

title: Cizîrê canton declares Democratic Autonomy
summary: The Cizîrê canton declared Democratic Autonomy and accepted the Social Contract, days before the Geneva II conference, as a political signal to international participants.

citation.quote: On three separate days, they issued their own declarations of Democratic Autonomy: on January 21 in Cizîrê, on January 27 in Kobanî, and on January 29 in Afrîn.

title: Kobanî canton declares autonomy
summary: Kobanî canton declared autonomy on January 27, 2014, with Enver Muslîm heading its executive council and Bêrîvan Hesen and Xalid Birgil as deputies.

citation.quote: Kobanî canton declared autonomy on January 27, 2014.

title: Kobanî canton declares Democratic Autonomy
summary: The Kobanî canton declared Democratic Autonomy and accepted the Social Contract, joining Cizîrê in asserting self-governance days before the Geneva II conference.

citation.quote: On three separate days, they issued their own declarations of Democratic Autonomy: on January 21 in Cizîrê, on January 27 in Kobanî, and on January 29 in Afrîn.

title: Afrîn canton declares Democratic Autonomy
summary: Afrîn canton declared Democratic Autonomy on January 29, 2014. The assembly elected Hêvî Îbrahîm Mustafa as board chair, who then appointed Remzi Şêxmus and Ebdil Hemid Mistefa as her deputies.

citation.quote: It declared Democratic Autonomy on January 29, 2014. The assembly elected Hêvî Îbrahîm Mustafa board chair, who in turn appointed Remzi Şêxmus and Ebdil Hemid Mistefa her deputies.

title: Rojava Social Contract adopted in the three cantons
summary: A commission compiled a draft Social Contract for the Democratic Autonomous Regions of Afrin, Jazira, and Kobane, affirming Democratic Autonomy, multicultural governance, gender equality, and a sweeping set of human rights guarantees.

citation.quote: Charter of the Social Contract, January 29, 2014, http://bit.ly/28PfEc2.

title: Afrîn canton declares Democratic Autonomy
summary: The Afrîn canton declared Democratic Autonomy and accepted the Social Contract, completing the three Rojava cantons' declarations. Hundreds of thousands celebrated in the streets.

citation.quote: On three separate days, they issued their own declarations of Democratic Autonomy: on January 21 in Cizîrê, on January 27 in Kobanî, and on January 29 in Afrîn. Hundreds of thousands of people celebrated in the streets of Rojava's cities.

title: KDP digs 20-mile trench along Rojava border
summary: The KDP decided to dig a 20-mile-long trench along its border with Rojava, ostensibly to defend against jihadists but in reality to prevent cross-border trade and tighten the embargo.

citation.quote: In February 2014, the KDP even decided to dig a 20-mile-long trench along its border with Rojava, ostensibly in defense against jihadists but in reality to prevent cross-border trade and to complete the embargo.

title: Medical Congress in Qamişlo discusses herbal healing
summary: A Medical Congress held in Qamişlo on March 2, 2014 discussed herbal healing methods, affirming the need to preserve the memory and legacy of traditional medicine and emphasizing bottom-up organization.

citation.quote: On March 2, 2014, a Medical Congress in Qamişlo discussed herbal healing methods, affirming the need to retain the memory and legacy of traditional medicine. It also emphasized bottom-up organization.

title: IS suicide attack on Qamişlo City Hall kills ten
summary: Two Islamic State suicide attackers shot guards, threw hand grenades into every room of the Qamişlo City Hall, killing ten staff and visitors including co-mayor Helepçe Xêlil, who was six months pregnant.

citation.chapter: Attack on the Qamişlo City Hall
citation.quote: We visited a small park in the Qamişlo neighborhood of Korniş, which was opened as a memorial to Helepçe Xêlil, who had been murdered in a bomb attack on the Qamişlo City Hall in April 2014.

title: Authors travel to Rojava to document the revolution firsthand
summary: In May 2014, the three authors set off on a journey to Rojava on behalf of the TATORT Kurdistan campaign to learn firsthand how the people of northern Syria were building a democratic society.

citation.quote: In May 2014, the three of us set off on a journey to Rojava to learn first-hand how the people of northern Syria were achieving the third way.

title: Authors cross into Rojava at Til Koçer border
summary: The authors entered Rojava from South Kurdistan (northern Iraq) via the Til Koçer border crossing, documenting conditions in the region firsthand.

citation.chapter: Prologue: On the Road to Til Koçer
citation.quote: In May 2014, it was not easy to cross the border from South Kurdistan (in northern Iraq) into Rojava. You could follow smugglers' and guerrillas' routes. Or you could cross at the town of Til Koçer (in Arabic, Al Yarubiya).

title: Syrian regime soldiers attack strategic points in Qamişlo
summary: Syrian government soldiers attempted to capture strategic positions in Qamişlo shortly before the authors' visit in May 2014, prompting a proportionate YPG/YPJ response.

citation.quote: One attack occurred just a few days before our visit to Qamişlo in May 2014, when Syrian soldiers wanted to capture some strategic points in the city, and another during our visit in Hesekê.

title: Kurdish women journalists of Rojava hold first conference in Qamişlo, founding RAJIN Rojava
summary: In May 2014, Kurdish women journalists of Rojava held their first conference in Qamişlo, where they founded the Kurdish Women's Press Association of Rojava (RAJIN Rojava). Seventy delegates attended, organized around the slogan honoring Gurbetelli Ersöz.

citation.quote: In May 2014, the Kurdish women journalists of Rojava held their first conference in Qamişlo, where they founded the Kurdish Women's Press Association of Rojava (RAJIN Rojava).

title: Authors visit Amûdê and meet Cizîrê DAA leadership
summary: The authors visited Amûdê in May 2014, five months after the declarations of Democratic Autonomy, meeting with Cizîrê co-president Ekram Hesso and several ministers of the transitional administration.

citation.quote: Our visit in May 2014 took place five months after the declarations of Democratic Autonomy. In Amûdê, we met with the Cizîrê co-president Ekram Hesso and several ministers.

title: Authors visit war-scarred Serêkaniyê during reconstruction
summary: The authors visited Serêkaniyê in May 2014, finding about 80 percent of the population had returned and the city was being rebuilt despite severe shortages and a trade embargo.

citation.quote: By the time we visited Serêkaniyê in May 2014, the war-scarred city was being rebuilt. About 80 percent of the population had returned and were trying to build a new life despite the terrible lack of supplies.

title: Bomb attack damages Serêkaniyê City Hall
summary: Two weeks before the authors' May 2014 arrival, a bomb attack damaged the Serêkaniyê City Hall, causing injuries and destruction witnessed in videos shown by staff.

citation.quote: Two weeks before we arrived, the City Hall had been damaged by a bomb attack. Everyone was still talking about it—the horror, the injuries. The staff showed us videos, taken afterward. We could see body parts strewn amid the destruction.

title: Delegation hears Öcalan's critique of organizing only in Kurdish areas
summary: Hanife Hisên explained to the authors' delegation in May 2014 that PKK leader Öcalan had criticized the YPG/YPJ for organizing self-defense units only in Kurdish areas rather than throughout Syria.

citation.chapter: 8.11 The Significance of the YPG and YPJ
citation.quote: Hanife Hisên explained to our delegation in May 2014 that PKK leader Öcalan had been critical on this point: "Why have you only organized in the Kurdish areas?"

title: Life imprisonment handed out twice in Cizîrê under Rojava justice system
summary: By May 2014, Rojava's new justice system had imposed its maximum penalty of life imprisonment (capped at twenty years) only twice in the Cizîrê canton — once for a man who murdered a woman, and once for a man who tortured and murdered a member of the Asayîş.

citation.quote: As of May 2014, this penalty had been handed out only twice in Cizîrê: once for a man who murdered a woman in a barbaric way, and once for a man who tortured and murdered a member of the Asayîş.

title: Asayîş resist regime advance on Hesekê, two killed
summary: When the authors arrived in Hesekê district in May 2014, Assad regime troops were advancing on the self-governed zone. Asayîş forces resisted the advance; two Asayîş were killed defending Hesekê's Kurdish neighborhood.

citation.quote: As soon as we arrived in Hesekê district in May 2014, we saw what they meant. Regime troops were trying to advance toward the self-governed zone, but the Asayîş were resisting them. Two Asayîş, among others, were killed while defending Hesekê's Kurdish neighborhood.

title: Authors' visit documents state of Rojava's education transformation
summary: As of the authors' May 2014 visit, the MGRK and education movement had not yet fully replaced former school leadership or transformed the system.

citation.quote: As of our May 2014 visit, the MGRK and the education movement had not entirely replaced the former school leadership, or transformed the system.

title: Kurdish Red Crescent employs 180 workers in Cizîrê canton
summary: As of May 2014, the Kurdish Red Crescent (HSK) had 180 employees in Cizîrê canton, helping health assemblies organize medical and humanitarian aid.

citation.quote: Kurdish Red Crescent (Heyva Sor a Kurdistanê, HSK), with 180 employees in Cizîrê canton (as of May 2014), helps the health assemblies organize medical and other humanitarian aid.

title: Rojava cantonal enterprise workers had not yet formed labor unions
summary: As of May 2014, workers in Rojava's district- and cantonal-level enterprises had not yet organized themselves into labor unions, despite the importance of strong workforce organization for fulfilling social tasks.

citation.quote: As of May 2014, they had not yet done so, but they must be encouraged.

title: Qamişlo municipal administration operating seven garbage vehicles
summary: As of May 2014, the Qamişlo municipal administration had seven vehicles available for waste collection, though they needed repairs and did not operate as effectively as needed.

citation.quote: As of May 2014, the Qamişlo municipal administration had seven vehicles available, but they didn't work as effectively as might be wished and needed repairs.

title: YPG commander at Til Xenzir reports captured jihadists thought they were fighting Israel
summary: In May 2014, the YPG commander at Til Xenzir, the westernmost YPG outpost in Cizîrê, recounted that some captured jihadists believed they had been fighting Israel, underscoring how disconnected IS recruits were from the actual conflict.

citation.quote: The commander at Til Xenzir, the westernmost YPG outpost in Cizîrê in May 2014, told us that some of the jihadists they captured thought they had been fighting Israel.

title: KDP shuts down border crossing at Til Koçer
summary: In late May 2014, the KDP closed the border crossing at Til Koçer, cutting off an entry point into Rojava.

citation.quote: In late May 2014, the KDP shut down the border crossing at Til Koçer, where we had entered Rojava.

title: Authors visit Serêkaniyê
summary: The authors visited Serêkaniyê, a predominantly Kurdish city on the western edge of Cizîrê canton, home to Kurds, Arabs, Syriacs, Armenians, and Chechens.

citation.quote: On May 11–13, 2014, we visited Serêkaniyê, a predominantly Kurdish city on the western edge of Cizîrê canton, home to Kurds, Arabs, Syriacs, Armenians, and Chechens.

title: Third conference of Young Revolutionary Women held in Rimelan, Cizîrê
summary: Around 230 young women from across the Cizîrê canton convened in Rimelan for the third conference of Young Revolutionary Women, assessing the previous year's work and setting new goals for women's liberation.

citation.quote: On May 16, 2014, one of the authors attended the third conference of Young Revolutionary Women in Cizîrê, held in Rimelan. Around 230 young women from all parts of the canton converged here to assess the work of the previous year and to set new goals for the coming year.

title: Second session of AZDW teacher training completed
summary: On May 26, 2014, the second session of teacher training at the AZDW was completed, following the academy's founding in fall 2013.

citation.quote: soon after our visit to the AZDW, on May 26, the second session of teacher training was completed.

title: ISIS kills fifteen people including seven children in Serêkaniyê region
summary: ISIS overran three villages in the Serêkaniyê region, slaughtering fifteen people including seven children. The villages were inhabited by Arab refugees, not Ezidis as ISIS claimed.

citation.quote: On May 29, 2014, it overran three villages in the Serêkaniyê region that were allegedly Ezidi but were actually inhabited by Arab refugees. ISIS slaughtered fifteen people, including seven children.

title: Movement between Kobanî and Afrîn cantons cut off
summary: By June 2014, the final overland link between the Rojava cantons was severed, leaving Cizîrê, Kobanî, Afrîn, and Aleppo each isolated and operating their councils separately.

citation.quote: movement between Kobanî and Afrîn remained possible until June 2014. Thereafter, the three cantons plus Aleppo were left on their own.

title: YPG and YPJ sign international conventions banning child recruitment and other violations
summary: The YPG and YPJ signed international conventions banning the acceptance of people under 18 into their ranks, along with conventions banning anti-personnel mines and sexual violence. A Geneva Call delegation subsequently visited Rojava to assess compliance.

citation.quote: In June 2014, the YPG and YPJ signed an international convention banning the acceptance of people under 18 into their ranks (and others banning anti-personnel mines and sexual violence).

title: ISIS captures Mosul, Iraq's second largest city
summary: ISIS seized Mosul, the commercial center of Iraq and the most important stop on the road to Syria, in June 2014.

citation.quote: In June 2014, it captured Iraq's second largest city, Mosul, the commercial center of Iraq and the most important stop on the road to Syria.

title: YPG declares readiness to defend South Kurdistan alongside Peshmerga
summary: The YPG sought to bury intramural hostilities and unite Kurds against the jihadists, declaring itself ready to fight alongside the Peshmerga and appealing to all peoples of Kurdistan to struggle against the common foe.

citation.quote: in June 2014, the YPG had declared itself ready to defend South Kurdistan alongside the Peshmerga.

title: Syrian presidential elections held; Rojava self-government boycotts
summary: In June 2014, Syrian presidential elections were held. While regime supporters in Qamişlo voted, Rojava's self-government boycotted the elections because the cantons did not recognize the regime so long as the regime did not recognize the cantons.

citation.quote: In June 2014 and in April 2016, when the Syrian presidential and parliamentary elections were held, regime supporters living in the neighborhoods of Qamişlo voted, but Rojava's self-government boycotted the elections on the grounds that the cantons did not recognize the regime as long as the regime didn't recognize the cantons.

title: ISIS mufti issues decree permitting rape of women in Mosul
summary: In Mosul, the ISIS mufti decreed that wives and daughters of soldiers and politicians working for the Maliki government were permissible targets for IS members, institutionalizing sexual violence as a weapon of war.

citation.quote: On June 18, 2014, in Mosul, the ISIS mufti decreed: "Wives and daughters of soldiers and politicians who work on behalf of Maliki are *halal* for members."

title: Human Rights Watch publishes report on Rojava Kurdish enclaves
summary: Human Rights Watch released a report titled "Syria: Abuses in Kurdish-Run Enclaves," confirming free access to prisons and institutions in Rojava.

citation.quote: "Syria: Abuses in Kurdish-Run Enclaves," Human Rights Watch, June 19, 2014, http://bit.ly/28R8s2N.

title: ISIS decrees laws restricting women in Turkmen villages
summary: On June 26, 2014, ISIS decreed a set of laws in Turkmen villages mandating full veiling, male escorts for women, and compelling families with two daughters to surrender one to IS.

citation.quote: Here are a few of the laws that ISIS decreed on June 26, 2014, in Turkmen villages:

title: ISIS renames itself Islamic State and proclaims worldwide caliphate
summary: On June 28, 2014, the first day of Ramadan, ISIS renamed itself Islamic State (IS) and declared itself the worldwide caliphate, invoking the Islamic expansion of the seventh and eighth centuries.

citation.quote: On June 28, the first day of Ramadan, it renamed itself Islamic State (IS) and proclaimed itself the worldwide caliphate, evoking the Islamic expansion in the seventh and eight centuries.

title: Cizîrê legislative council introduces mandatory conscription
summary: Due to the deteriorating security situation, Cizîrê's legislative council instituted conscription requiring men aged 18–30 to complete six months of basic military service, with voluntary participation for women.

citation.quote: On July 7, 2014, due to the ominous situation in Cizîrê, the legislative council introduced conscription: all men (initially) between the ages of 18 and 30 now have to complete six months of basic military service.

title: Azize Aslan speaks at DTK's Democratic Economy conference in Amed
summary: Azize Aslan delivered a speech at the DTK's 'Democratic Economy' conference in Amed, critiquing capitalism's focus on exchange value and profit and advocating for an economy oriented toward society rather than the market.

citation.quote: Azize Aslan, speech to the DTK's "Democratic Economy" conference, Amed, reported in "Hedef Komünal bir Ekonomi," *Özgur Gündem*, July 14, 2014, http://bit.ly/1DA8Ewu.

title: IS captures more than 7,000 Ezidi and Christian women
summary: In August 2014, IS attacked Ezidi and Christian villages and cities, capturing more than 7,000 women whom they repeatedly raped, sold at slave markets, or gave to jihadists as war booty.

citation.quote: In August 2014, IS attacked Ezidi and Christian villages and cities and captured more than 7,000 women. They repeatedly raped them, then sold them at slave markets as chattels; they gave them over to jihadists as war booty or forced them to marry.

title: IS attacks Maxmur; PKK fighters repel the jihadists
summary: Islamic State attacked the refugee camp at Maxmur, bringing Hewlêr into danger. KDP Peshmerga fled, but PKK fighters were able to repel the IS assault.

citation.quote: In August 2014, IS attacked Maxmur, bringing Hêwler into danger. KDP Peshmerga failed to fend off the jihadists and fled. Only the PKK fighters were able to repel them.

title: PKK supports PUK Peshmerga in defense of Kirkuk
summary: PKK fighters supported PUK Peshmerga in successfully defending the multi-ethnic city of Kirkuk against the Islamic State advance.

citation.quote: The PKK supported PUK Peshmerga in the successful defense of the multi-ethnic metropolis of Kirkuk.

title: IS attacks and occupies Şengal, massacring and enslaving Ezidis
summary: IS attacked Şengal city, murdering and enslaving thousands of Ezidis and capturing thousands of women and girls. Tens of thousands fled to nearby Mount Şengal.

citation.quote: On August 3, 2014, IS attacked Şengal city and occupied it. It murdered or enslaved thousands of Ezidis and captured and enslaved thousands of women and girls.

title: YPG, YPJ, and PKK open corridor to rescue 200,000 Ezidis from Mount Şengal
summary: After Ezidis fled to Mount Şengal and were trapped without food or supplies, the YPG, YPJ, and PKK opened a protective corridor and rescued 200,000 of them, bringing them to Cizîrê canton.

citation.quote: As horror mounted, the YPG, the YPJ, and the PKK opened a protective corridor for the trapped Ezidis and rescued 200,000 of them, bringing them to Cizîrê.

title: Rojava defense forces defeat Islamic State at Kobanî
summary: Between September 2014 and January 2015, Rojava's defense forces waged a stunning resistance to the Islamic State at Kobanî and defeated it, drawing world attention to the revolution.

citation.quote: Then, between September 2014 and January 2015, the revolution's defense forces waged a stunning resistance to the Islamic State (IS) at Kobanî—and defeated it.

title: IS launches major offensive on Kobanî city
summary: In mid-September 2014, IS Islamist militias commenced a major offensive on Kobanî city. Isolated from other cantons and surrounded by enemies, most of the population fled, leaving only fighters to defend the city.

citation.quote: In mid-September 2014, the Islamist militias commenced another major offensive on the city. Isolated from Afrîn and Cizîrê, Kobanî was surrounded by enemies.

title: IS attack on Kobanî prompts formation of HPC defense committees
summary: Following the Islamic State attack on Kobanî in September 2014, local people systematically formed defense committees called HPC (Society Defense Forces) to serve as a first line of neighborhood defense.
