citation.quote: After the IS attack on Kobanî in September 2014, local people systematically formed defense committees called HPC (Hêzên Parastina Cewherî—Society Defense Forces).

title: Kurdish-language instruction offered in Arab-majority schools in new school year
summary: When the new school year started in September 2014, Kurdish-language instruction was offered in schools with mainly Arab students, following their request.

citation.quote: When the new school year started in September 2014, it was offered in these schools.

title: IS attack on Kobanî derails Kurdish-language school preparations
summary: The Islamic State's assault on Kobanî in September 2014 cut short preparations that had begun to introduce Kurdish-language instruction in the canton's schools.

citation.chapter: 10.3 The Academy for Kurdish Language, History, and Literature (AZDW)
citation.quote: (In Kobanî, preparations had begun, but the IS attack in September 2014 jettisoned all such plans.)

title: IS circulates videos showing shootings of pedestrians and drivers
summary: In September 2014, videos spread online showing IS members shooting pedestrians and drivers from moving cars, with jihad battle songs playing in the background.

citation.quote: In September 2014, videos circulated over the Internet, showing IS people in moving cars shooting pedestrians and drivers with semi-automatic weapons, while nasheed (battle songs, in this case for jihad) played in the background.

title: IS launches assault on Kobanî canton
summary: Islamic State attacked the self-governing canton of Kobanî with modern weapons including heavy arms looted from US stores in Mosul and some fifty tanks, quickly overrunning more than three hundred villages and part of the city.

citation.quote: On September 15, 2014, IS attacked the self-governing canton of Kobanî, with the goal of taking over all of northern Syria. They used modern weapons systems, including heavy weapons looted from US stores in Mosul and some fifty tanks.

title: IS destroys Armenian genocide memorial at Deir ez-Zor
summary: On September 21, 2014, the Islamic State (IS) destroyed the Armenian Apostolic Church's genocide memorial complex in Deir ez-Zor, which had been a major site of pilgrimage for Armenians worldwide.

citation.quote: But on September 21, 2014, IS destroyed it.

title: 60 Minutes Australia airs "Female State" documentary on YPJ
summary: The Australian television program 60 Minutes broadcast a documentary called "Female State" (also titled "Women of the YPJ"), bringing global attention to women fighters in Rojava.

citation.quote: "Women of the YPJ/Female State," 60 Minutes Australia, September 28, 2014.

title: Marie Claire publishes feature on women fighting ISIS
summary: Marie Claire magazine published a multi-page report by Elizabeth Griffin on YPJ fighters, bringing international mainstream media attention to the women of Rojava.

citation.quote: Elizabeth Griffin, "These Remarkable Women Are Fighting ISIS, and It's Time You Know Who They Are," Marie Claire, September 30, 2014.

title: Popular uprising in Turkey in solidarity with Kobanî war
summary: Supporters of the Rojava Revolution mounted a widespread popular uprising in Turkey in October 2014 during the Kobanî war, to which the Turkish state and its counterinsurgency forces reacted harshly.

citation.quote: When supporters of the Rojava Revolution mounted a widespread popular uprising in October 2014, during the Kobanî war, the Turkish state and its counterinsurgency forces reacted harshly.

title: Kurdish lawyer asserts genocide of Armenians and Syriacs continues in Turkey
summary: At the Frankfurt Book Fair in October 2014, Kurdish lawyer Mahmut Şakar declared that the genocide of Armenians and Syriacs in Turkey was ongoing.

citation.quote: In October 2014, at the Frankfurt Book Fair, the Kurdish lawyer Mahmut Şakar asserted that the genocide of the Armenians and Syriacs in Turkey continues today.

title: Syriac parties convene in Cizîrê and agree on cooperation
summary: All Syriac parties convened in Cizîrê in October 2014 and agreed on close cooperation, including support for the Sutoro and the Syriac Military Council.

citation.quote: In October 2014, all the Syriac parties convened in Cizîrê and agreed on close cooperation. They all wanted to support the Sutoro and the Syriac Military Council—even the Chaldeans, who didn't approve of independent security forces.

title: Radio report: 50 percent of Rojava women received weapons training
summary: Journalist Berfîn Hezîl reported in an October 2014 radio interview that approximately 50 percent of all women of every age in Rojava had received weapons training.

citation.quote: The journalist Berfîn Hezîl reported in a radio interview in October 2014 that some 50 percent of all women of every age in Rojava had received weapons training.

title: First contingent of KDP Peshmerga arrives in Kobanî
summary: Erdoğan twice allowed about 140 KDP Peshmerga fighters with some heavy weapons to travel through Turkey; the first group arrived in October 2014 to join the YPG, YPJ, and Burkan Al-Firat in defending Kobanî.

citation.quote: Erdoğan, pressed to provide help, twice allowed about 140 KDP Peshmerga to travel through Turkey with a few heavy weapons for the defense of Kobanî. Arriving in October and December 2014, they joined the YPG, the YPJ, and Burkan Al-Firat in defending Kobanî.

title: US-led coalition collaborates in defense of Kobanî
summary: In October 2014, public pressure forced the US-led coalition against IS to collaborate in the defense of Kobanî in a limited way, a development welcomed by people in Rojava.

citation.quote: Another debate emerged among leftists in October 2014, when public opinion forced the US-led coalition against IS to collaborate in the defense of Kobanî in a limited way.

title: Turkish state attacks Kobanî solidarity demonstrators, killing over forty
summary: As millions demonstrated in Turkish and Kurdish cities to protest government silence on Kobanî, the Turkish state attacked protesters brutally over three days, killing more than forty people.

citation.quote: On October 6–8, the Turkish state attacked the demonstrators brutally, killing more than forty.

title: Die Welt publishes article on Kurdish secular resistance
summary: The German bourgeois newspaper Die Welt published an article observing that the Kurds, men and women equally, had become a serious secular actor in the Middle East, citing progress in civil society.

citation.quote: "Der kurdische Widerstand verkörpert das Gute," Die Welt, October 18, 2014.

title: Dohuk Agreement on power-sharing signed between ENKS and Rojava self-government
summary: The Dohuk Agreement established a power-sharing arrangement between the ENKS and the Rojava self-government, as part of a broader united front against IS.

citation.quote: recently even the ENKS has had no choice but to work with the Rojava self-government, as laid out in the power-sharing Dohuk Agreement in October 22, 2014.

title: Barzanî relaxes embargo and allows goods into Rojava
summary: Under US pressure during the battle for Kobanî, Barzanî relaxed the KRG embargo somewhat and allowed some goods to pass over the border into Rojava.

citation.quote: In November 2014, Barzanî relaxed the embargo somewhat, and the KRG allowed some goods to pass over the border into Rojava.

title: Global demonstrations in solidarity with Rojava
summary: On November 1, 2014, people across the world — from Berlin to Melbourne, from Tehran to Kabul — took to the streets in demonstrations expressing solidarity with the Rojava revolution and the defense of Kobanî.

citation.quote: For the defenders of Kobanî, it had great meaning that on November 1, 2014, from Berlin to Melbourne, from Tehran to Kabul, people poured into the streets to demonstrate on behalf of Rojava.

title: Dr. Ahmad Yousef calls for alternative economy in ANF interview
summary: Dr. Ahmad Yousef, speaking in an ANF interview on November 9, 2014, argued that capitalist economic policy widens the gap between rich and poor and called for an alternative economy oriented toward the just redistribution of wealth.

citation.quote: Dr. Ahmad Yousef, in *ANF*, November 9, 2014.

title: Second contingent of KDP Peshmerga arrives in Kobanî
summary: A second group of KDP Peshmerga with heavy weapons arrived in December 2014 through Turkey to reinforce the defenders of Kobanî alongside the YPG, YPJ, and Burkan Al-Firat.

citation.quote: Erdoğan, pressed to provide help, twice allowed about 140 KDP Peshmerga to travel through Turkey with a few heavy weapons for the defense of Kobanî. Arriving in October and December 2014, they joined the YPG, the YPJ, and Burkan Al-Firat in defending Kobanî.

title: Rojava Revolution establishes armed feminist direct democracy
summary: By 2015 an armed feminist uprising demanding direct democracy had emerged across a significant swath of the Middle East, surprising nearly all outside observers.

citation.quote: If one had told almost anyone who wasn't part of the Kurdish movement in 2010 that by 2015 there would be an armed feminist uprising demanding direct democracy across a significant swath of the Middle East, they would probably have thought you were insane. Yet there it is.

title: Liberation of Girê Spî, Hesekê, Tishrin Dam; creation of Syrian Democratic Forces and Council
summary: In 2015–16, the liberation of Girê Spî, Hesekê, and the Tishrin Dam, along with the creation of the Syrian Democratic Forces and Syrian Democratic Council and the Manbij operation, demonstrated that Democratic Autonomy could be a feasible alternative for all of Syria.

citation.quote: In 2015–16, the liberation of Girê Spî (Til Abyad), Hesekê, and the Tishrin Dam, the creation of the Syrian Democratic Forces and the Syrian Democratic Council, and the Manbij operation suggested that the system could be a feasible alternative for all of Syria.

title: Massacres in Amed and Suruç amid attacks on Kurdish and leftist people
summary: That summer, massacres in Amed (Diyarbakir) and Suruç (at the border to Kobanî), along with hundreds of other attacks, paved the way for a brutal war against Turkey's free Kurdish and leftist-democratic people.

citation.quote: That summer massacres in Amed (Diyarbakir) and Suruç (at the border to Kobanî), along with hundreds of other attacks, paved the way for a brutal war against Turkey's free Kurdish and leftist-democratic people.

title: Janet Biehl publishes "Two Academies in Rojava"
summary: Janet Biehl published "Two Academies in Rojava" on Biehlonbookchin.com in 2015, documenting the women's academies in Rojava.

citation.chapter: Women’s Education and Research Centers—Navenda Perwerde û Zanist Jinê
citation.quote: Janet Biehl, “Two Academies in Rojava,” Biehlonbookchin.com], 2015

title: Communes in Cizîre canton exceed 1,600
summary: By the end of 2015, the number of communes in Cizîre canton had grown to over 1,600, with efforts continuing to establish communes in villages and streets not yet organized.

citation.quote: At the end of 2015, the number of communes in Cizîre canton exceeded 1,600. Many villages and residential streets still do not have communes, so efforts continue to establish them.

title: Girê Spî council votes to join Kobanî canton
summary: After months of discussion, the newly formed Girê Spî council chose at the end of 2015 to become part of Kobanî canton rather than establish its own separate canton.

citation.quote: After several months of discussion, a council in Girê Spî was established with the participation of all parts of society. This council discussed forming its own canton, but at the end of 2015 it chose to become part of Kobanî canton.

title: Jihadist attacks resume on self-governed parts of Aleppo
summary: Since early 2015, the self-governed parts of Aleppo came under repeated attack from jihadists, including the new coalition Jaish Al-Fatah led by Al-Nusra (Al-Qaeda) and heavily supported by Turkey.

citation.quote: Since early 2015, the self-governed parts of Aleppo have repeatedly come under attack from jihadists. The new coalition Jaish Al-Fatah, led by Al-Nusra (Al-Qaeda) and heavily supported by Turkey, is continually trying to conquer the liberated parts of Aleppo, but the people of Şêx Maqsûd are maintaining their self-defense.

title: Expanded road blacktopping in and around Cizîrê cities
summary: In 2015, many more roads in and around the cities of Cizîrê canton were blacktopped, reflecting continued improvement in municipal infrastructure under the people's municipalities.

citation.quote: In 2014, quite a few potholes in the city streets and on the main roads were filled in with asphalt. In 2015, many more roads in and around the cities of Cizîrê were blacktopped.

title: Cizîre and Afrîn cantons adopt mandatory dual co-head leadership
summary: In summer 2015, Cizîre and Afrîn decided their cantonal governments must have both a woman and a man as co-heads. Sheikh Hamedi Daham and Hediye Yusîv led Cizîre; Osman Sheikh joined Hevî Mustafa in Afrîn.

citation.quote: In the summer of 2015, Cizîre and Afrîn decided that from that point onward their cantonal governments must have a woman and a man as co-heads.

title: Organization of communes in Afrîn canton completed
summary: The organization of communes in Afrîn canton was completed in summer 2015, while commune organization in Kobanî restarted following the defeat of Islamic State.

citation.quote: The organization of communes in Afrîn canton was completed in summer 2015, while in Kobanî it restarted after the defeat of IS.

title: Process discussion held on MGRK–DAA relationship
summary: In summer 2015, a formal process discussion was held to seek a common solution to the question of how the MGRK council system and the DAAs should be formally integrated, with a 40 percent quota formula discussed in early 2016.

citation.quote: In this regard, in the summer of 2015, a process discussion was held, looking for a common solution.

title: Afrîn canton institutes local conscription with first 200 youths
summary: In early 2015, Afrîn canton established its own conscription program, enrolling an initial cohort of 200 youths over age 18 into self-defense units (erka xweparastinê) separate from the YPG/YPJ.

citation.quote: In Afrîn canton, conscription was instituted in early 2015 with the first 200 youths over age 18.

title: Defense commissions establish civilian self-defense units in village and neighborhood communes
summary: Also in early 2015, defense commissions systematically created civilian self-defense units (hêzen parastina cewherî) in village and neighborhood communes throughout Rojava, tasked with street monitoring and supporting the Asayîş.

citation.quote: Also in early 2015, the defense commissions systematically established self-defense units (hêzen parastina cewherî) in the village and neighborhood communes, comprising civilians of every age.

title: YPG/YPJ clear Hesekê of jihadists, cutting IS route between Mosul and Raqqa
summary: The YPG and YPJ cleared Hesekê of jihadist forces, depriving IS of direct control over the route between Mosul and Raqqa.

citation.quote: Then when the YPG/YPJ cleared Hesekê of jihadists in the summer of 2015, it lost direct control over the route between Mosul and Raqqa.

title: Al-Sanadid Forces founded by Sheikh Hamidi Daham
summary: The Al-Sanadid Forces, a militia of the Şammar tribe, were founded in early 2015 by tribal leader Sheikh Hamidi Daham to support the YPG/YPJ in the fight against IS.

citation.quote: Al-Sanadid was founded in early 2015 by the tribal leader Sheikh Hamidi Daham, to support the YPG/YPJ in the struggle against IS.

title: Decision made to establish justice platforms in Rojava
summary: A long discussion in summer 2015 concluded that greater public participation was needed for resolving conflicts at the community level, leading to the establishment of justice platforms assembling up to 300 people.

citation.quote: A long discussion in summer 2015 came to the conclusion that greater public participation was needed for resolving conflicts at the community level. To this end, the decision was made to establish "justice platforms."

title: Majority of Syriac children in Rojava taught in native Aramaic tongue
summary: During the 2015 school term, the majority of Syriac children in Rojava were being taught in their native Aramaic tongue.

citation.quote: Meanwhile during the 2015 school term, the majority of Syriac children in Rojava were taught in their native tongue.

title: Most primary schools in Afrîn switch to Kurdish-medium teaching
summary: Two years after the 2013 pilot, most primary schools in Afrîn adopted Kurdish as the primary language of instruction, with mathematics, sports, handicrafts, and history-social studies all taught in Kurdish.

citation.chapter: 10.3 The Academy for Kurdish Language, History, and Literature (AZDW)
citation.quote: Two years later, most primary schools in Afrîn decided to teach mostly in Kurdish. … In Afrîn, mathematics, sports, handicrafts, and history-social studies have been taught in Kurdish for more than two years.

title: First book published in Rojava
summary: At the end of 2015 the first book was published in Rojava, marking a milestone in the region's development of an independent education policy.

citation.chapter: 10.3 The Academy for Kurdish Language, History, and Literature (AZDW)
citation.quote: It was only at the end of 2015 that the first book was published in Rojava, a harbinger of a full independent education policy.

title: Women's Education and Science Academy re-established in Kobanî
summary: Several academies, including the Women's Education and Science Academy, were re-established in Kobanî in 2015 following the IS occupation, supporting activist women in the region.

citation.quote: Several academies were also re-established in 2015, like the Women's Education and Science Academy, important for activist women.

title: Serêkaniyê hospital re-equipped after Al-Nusra looting
summary: The hospital in Serêkaniyê had been looted when Al-Nusra occupied the city, but its re-equipment was organized in 2015.

citation.quote: The hospital in Serêkaniyê was looted when Al-Nusra occupied the city, but its re-equipment was organized in 2015.

title: Over 2,500 hectares redistributed to councils in Serêkaniyê
summary: In 2015, more than 2,500 hectares of formerly state-owned land were redistributed to councils in Serêkaniyê alone as part of Rojava's cooperative land reform.

citation.quote: In 2015, more than 2,500 hectares of formerly state-owned land were redistributed to the councils in Serêkaniyê alone, and more will follow.

title: Cizîrê cooperatives plant 50,000 fruit trees
summary: In 2015, cooperatives in Cizîrê planted 50,000 fruit trees as part of efforts to diversify agriculture by ecological criteria and break the wheat monoculture.

citation.quote: In Cizîrê, cooperatives planted 50,000 fruit trees in 2015 and attempts are being made to diversify agriculture by ecological criteria and to change the wheat monoculture.

title: Network of small cooperatives established across Cizîrê
summary: By the end of 2015, a network of small cooperatives spanning bread-baking, textiles, dairy, and other sectors had spread across Cizîrê.

citation.quote: By the end of 2015, a network of small cooperatives dotted Cizîrê.

title: Debates over building ecological-democratic factories in Rojava
summary: As of late 2015, discussions were underway in Rojava on how to construct ecological, democratic, and communal factories to cover all social needs, though the embargo and ongoing attacks made progress difficult.

citation.quote: As of late 2015, debates are taking place over how to build ecological, democratic, and communal factories. Ideas for the construction of ecological-democratic industry are being developed to cover all social needs.

title: First Ecology Academy founded in Cizîrê
summary: To spread ecological awareness across Rojava, the first Ecology Academy was established in the Cizîrê canton in 2015.

citation.quote: In 2015, to spread ecological awareness, the first Ecology Academy was founded in Cizîrê.

title: KRG imposes embargo on Mount Şengal to prevent declaration of Democratic Autonomy
summary: For several months in 2015, the KRG embargoed Mount Şengal to prevent the local population from declaring Democratic Autonomy, with KDP Peshmerga blocking roads to keep other Kurdish forces away.

citation.quote: For a few months in 2015, the KRG put Mount Şengal under an embargo to prevent the people from declaring Democratic Autonomy. KDP Peshmerga blocked roads to keep the other Kurdish forces away from the region, and tightened the embargo again.

title: Al-Nusra and Turkish troops attack Afrîn
summary: In 2015, Al-Nusra, operating as part of the Jaish Al-Fatah alliance, along with Turkish troops, attacked the Kurdish canton of Afrîn in northern Syria.

citation.quote: In 2015, Al-Nusra, as part of the Jaish Al-Fatah alliance, as well as Turkish troops, attacked Afrîn.

title: Jaish Al-Fatah jihadist alliance formed
summary: Jaish Al-Fatah (Army of Conquest) was formed in 2015 as a jihadist alliance led by Jabhat Al-Nusra and Ahrar Al-Sham, with support from Turkey, Saudi Arabia, and Qatar.

citation.quote: Jaish Al-Fatah (Army of Conquest), formed in 2015, is a jihadist alliance led by Jabhat Al-Nusra and Ahrar Al-Sham, both affiliated with Al-Qaeda.

title: Turkmen militias formed under Sultan Murat Brigade banner
summary: Turkmen militias were formed in 2015, eventually comprising about 10,000 fighters including Turkish military veterans, special forces, and far-right cadres, operating under the Sultan Murat Brigade with backing from Turkey, Saudi Arabia, and the KDP.

citation.quote: Turkmen militias were formed in 2015 and now comprise about 10,000 fighters, mainly Turkish military veterans, special forces, and far-right cadres.

title: Rojava's defense forces defeat IS at Kobanî
summary: The defense forces of Rojava achieved a major victory at Kobanî in 2015, inflicting the first major defeat on IS and opening a new chapter for the region.

citation.quote: Its defense forces' victory at Kobanî in 2015, however, opened a whole new chapter. Even as conditions in the rest of Syria deteriorated, Rojava had moved forward and inflicted the first major defeat on IS.

title: YPG/YPJ liberate Kobanî and drive IS from the area
summary: In January 2015, the YPG/YPJ liberated Kobanî city and drove IS from the area, ending the siege that had drawn global attention and US-led coalition air strikes.

citation.quote: In January 2015, the YPG/YPJ liberated Kobanî and drove IS from the area.

title: YPG/YPJ victory at Kobanî
summary: In January 2015, the YPG/YPJ and their allies achieved victory at Kobanî, further strengthening Arab support for the Kurdish defense forces.

citation.quote: With every victory achieved by the YPG/YPJ and their allies—at Kobanî (January 2015), at Til Hemîs (February 2015), at Girê Spî (June 2015), and at Şengal und Hol (November 2015)—Arab support for the YPG grows stronger.

title: Kobanî liberated after four months of fighting
summary: After four months of intense combat, Kobanî liberated itself from IS on January 27; most of the 365 surrounding villages were freed within days, though at least five hundred YPG/YPJ fighters had been killed and roughly 80 percent of the city's buildings destroyed.

citation.quote: On January 27, after four months of heavy fighting, Kobanî liberated itself. After only a few more days, most of the 365 villages were freed.

title: YPG/YPJ liberate Til Hemîs in joint Kurdish-Arab operation
summary: In February 2015, the YPG/YPJ liberated Til Hemîs in a joint Kurdish-Arab operation, with nearby Til Barak liberated a month later in March 2015.

citation.quote: Not until February 2015 did the YPG/YPJ liberate Til Hemîs, and nearby Til Barak a month later—in a joint Kurdish-Arab operation.

title: YPG/YPJ liberate Til Barak
summary: In March 2015, approximately one month after the liberation of Til Hemîs, the YPG/YPJ liberated nearby Til Barak in a joint Kurdish-Arab operation.

citation.quote: Not until February 2015 did the YPG/YPJ liberate Til Hemîs, and nearby Til Barak a month later—in a joint Kurdish-Arab operation.

title: District municipal parliament elections held in Cizîre canton
summary: On March 13, 2015, elections for the "district municipal parliament" were carried out across twelve districts of Cizîre canton, excluding Til Temir where IS made voting impossible.

citation.quote: On March 13, 2015, elections were carried out in Cizîre canton, in twelve districts (though in Til Temir this was impossible, due to IS). These elections were held for the "district municipal parliament."

title: Jaish Al-Fatah captures Syrian city of Idlib
summary: Jaish Al-Fatah captured the Syrian city of Idlib on March 28, 2015, and proceeded to take much of the province in the area around Aleppo and Afrîn.

citation.quote: It captured the Syrian city of Idlib on March 28, 2015, and much of the province thereafter, in the area around Aleppo and Afrîn.

title: Turkish elections give HDP seats in parliament
summary: In June 2015, Turkish elections saw the pro-Kurdish and left Peoples' Democratic Party (HDP) overcome the 10 percent threshold and win many seats in the Turkish Parliament.

citation.quote: In June 2015, Turkish elections were held, and citizens who supported a democratic alliance of peoples turned out to the polls in huge numbers, enough to overcome the 10 percent threshold and give the pro-Kurdish and left Peoples' Democratic Party (HDP) many seats in the Turkish Parliament.

title: YPG/YPJ and Burkan Al-Firat liberate Girê Spî (Til Abyad)
summary: In June 2015, the YPG/YPJ and Burkan Al-Firat (an FSA group) liberated Girê Spî (Til Abyad), establishing a mixed Kurdish, Arab, and Turkmen self-administration and annexing the area to Kobanî canton, closing the gap between Cizîrê and Kobanî cantons.

citation.quote: In June 2015 the YPG/YPJ and Burkan Al-Firat (an FSA group) liberated Girê Spî (in Arabic, Til Abyad), which lay between Cizîrê and Kobanî cantons.

title: YPG/YPJ victory at Girê Spî
summary: In June 2015, the YPG/YPJ and allies achieved victory at Girê Spî, continuing a string of victories that strengthened Arab support for the Kurdish defense forces.

citation.quote: With every victory achieved by the YPG/YPJ and their allies—at Kobanî (January 2015), at Til Hemîs (February 2015), at Girê Spî (June 2015), and at Şengal und Hol (November 2015)—Arab support for the YPG grows stronger.

title: YPG/YPJ liberate Girê Spî
summary: The YPG/YPJ liberated Girê Spî. Amnesty International subsequently reported that the YPG had expelled Turkmens and local Arabs from the area, an accusation rebutted by the Syrian Kurdish Human Rights Association.

citation.quote: After the YPG/YPJ liberated Girê Spî in June 2015, Amnesty International reported that the YPG had expelled Turkmens and local Arabs from that area.

title: YPG/YPJ liberate Girê Spî, connecting Kobanî and Cizîre cantons
summary: In June 2015, YPG and YPJ forces liberated Girê Spî (Til Abyad) and surrounding areas, geographically reconnecting Kobanî and Cizîre cantons for the first time since 2013.

citation.quote: In June 2015, the YPG/YPJ forces liberated Girê Spî (Til Abyad) and its surroundings, which geographically connected Kobanî and Cizîre cantons.

title: YPG/YPJ liberates Girê Spî (Til Abyad) from IS
summary: Kurdish forces liberated Girê Spî (Til Abyad) from Islamic State, after which Turkey cut electricity to the city. Turkey had previously supplied electricity while IS held the city.

citation.quote: We saw that clearly in October 2015, in a visit to the newly liberated city of Girê Spî (Til Abyad). Turkey had formerly provided electricity to the city, but once the YPG/YPJ liberated it in June 2015, it cut the electricity.

title: HDP wins 13 percent in Turkish parliamentary elections
summary: On June 7, 2015, the HDP surpassed Turkey's 10 percent electoral threshold with 13 percent of the vote, gaining parliamentary representation and positioning itself to challenge Erdoğan's presidential ambitions.

citation.quote: In the Turkish parliamentary elections on June 7, 2015, the HDP easily overcame the 10 percent threshold, gaining 13 percent of the vote.

title: YPG/YPJ liberate Girê Spî (Til Abyad), connecting Cizîrê and Kobanî
summary: The YPG/YPJ liberation of Girê Spî geographically connected the Cizîrê and Kobanî cantons, representing a setback for Turkey's AKP government and its neo-Ottoman ambitions against the Kurdish movement.

citation.quote: The YPG/YPJ liberation of Girê Spî (Til Abyad) on June 16, 2015, was a setback for the AKP, because the result was to geographically connect Cizîrê and Kobanî.

title: Yekîtiya Star establishes all-women commune in Til Temir
summary: Yekîtiya Star established an all-women commune in Til Temir, part of the broader expansion of women's communes across Rojava's Arab and Kurdish neighborhoods.

citation.quote: "Yekîtiya Star Establishes All-Women Commune in Til Temir," ANHA Hawar News, June 26, 2015.

title: IS massacre kills over 288 civilians in Kobanî
summary: Two IS groups attacked Kobanî from the south while a third entered directly through the Turkish border crossing at Murşitpinar, with fighters wearing YPG uniforms killing more than 288 civilians, many of them children, in a deliberate terror campaign.

citation.quote: On June 26, 2015, two groups of IS attacked Kobanî from the south while a third group entered the city directly through the Turkish border post of Murşitpinar. Their goal was to gain control of the city, supported by thousands of IS fighters from across the Euphrates River to the west.

title: Women establish commune center in Efrîn
summary: Women established a new commune center in Efrîn, reflecting the rapid spread of women's self-organization in Rojava's cantons.

citation.quote: "Women Establish Commune Center in Efrîn," ANHA Hawar News, June 29, 2015.

title: Turkey declares Euphrates River a red line for YPG
summary: In July 2015, Turkey declared the Euphrates River a red line, threatening military attack if the YPG/YPJ crossed into Manbij.

citation.quote: In July 2015, Turkey stipulated that the Euphrates River was a "red line" across which the YPG/YPJ could not advance into Manbij. Should the Syrian Kurds dare to cross the river, they would be attacked by the Turkish military.

title: Cizîrê Health Congress votes to open a health academy
summary: The Cizîrê Health Congress, held in Dirbesiyê in mid-September 2015, decided to open a health academy and establish educational committees in each health sector to improve health education quality.

citation.quote: In mid-September 2015, the Cizîrê Health Congress, held in Dirbesiyê, decided to open a health academy and to establish educational committees in each health sector, thus improving the quality of health education.

title: Druze city of As Suwayda declares democratic self-administration
summary: In September 2015, the Druze city of As Suwayda in southern Syria declared its own democratic self-administration, with delegations traveling to Rojava to exchange support and information.

citation.quote: in September 2015, the Druze city of As Suwayda, in southern Syria, declared its own democratic self-administration, and delegations from As Suwayda traveled to Rojava to exchange support and information.

title: Bethnahrin Women Protection Forces founded
summary: The Bethnahrin Women Protection Forces was formed as a Syriac women's armed force to fight for women's rights and act in solidarity with women of other nations, taking inspiration from the YPJ.

citation.quote: In September 2015, the Bethnahrin Women Protection Forces was formed. "Along with the MFS and Sutoro, we needed a women's force," said a spokesperson. They aim to "improve the values of Syriac people, fight for women's rights, act in solidarity with women of other nations, and struggle against the forces of reaction."

title: Syrian Democratic Forces founded
summary: The Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) were founded in October 2015, with the Turkmen Lîwa Al-Selcuki participating alongside Kurdish and Arab groups.

citation.quote: When the Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) were founded in October 2015, the Turkmen Lîwa Al-Selcuki participated.

title: Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) established
summary: Military successes in Cizîre and Kobanî cantons in October 2015 led to the establishment of the Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF), broadening the military coalition beyond the original three cantons.

citation.quote: In October 2015, military successes in Cizîre and Kobanî cantons led to the establishment of the Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF).

title: Turkish Army attacks YPG fighters attempting to cross Euphrates
summary: In late October 2015, when YPG fighters showed signs of crossing the Euphrates by boat toward Manbij, the Turkish Army attacked them several times.

citation.quote: So in late October 2015, when YPG fighters showed signs of crossing the Euphrates in boats, the Turkish Army attacked several times.

title: Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) formed
summary: The Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) were formed in October 2015, becoming a beacon of hope for the region by uniting Arabs, Syriacs, Turkmens, and Kurds.

citation.quote: The formation of the SDF in October 2015 and the Syrian Democratic Council (MDS) in December 2015 is a beacon of hope for the whole region.

title: IS massacre of 102 peace protesters in Turkey
summary: On October 10, 2015, the Islamic State massacred 102 peace protesters in Turkey, the culmination of a hateful and racist campaign by the AKP government against the HDP and Kurdish movement.

citation.quote: culminating on October 10, 2015, in a massacre by IS of 102 peace protesters.

title: Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) founded
summary: The SDF, an umbrella military alliance of thirty forces including the YPG/YPJ, was announced in October 2015, uniting Kurds, Arabs, Syriacs, and other Syrian ethnicities to fight IS and build a democratic Syria.

citation.quote: On October 10, 2015, the formation of the Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF; in Arabic, Qūwāt Sūriyā ad-dīmuqrāṭya; in Kurdish, Hêzên Sûriya Demokratîk) was announced.

title: Lower-level municipal elections held in Afrîn canton
summary: On October 11, 2015, elections were held at the lower (non-district) levels in Afrîn canton, with independent election commissions overseeing the first genuinely free elections ever held in Rojava or Syria.

citation.quote: On October 11, 2015, in Afrîn canton, elections were held at the lower levels (not district level). Independent election commissions were created.

title: Kobanî canton passes binding women's laws
summary: Kobanî canton passed a set of women's laws binding on everyone in the canton, including a ban on childhood marriage.

citation.quote: But on October 27, 2015, Kobanî passed a set of women's laws that are binding on everyone in the canton, banning childhood marriage among other things.

title: YPG/YPJ victory at Şengal and Hol
summary: In November 2015, the YPG/YPJ and allies achieved victory at Şengal and Hol, further expanding their area of control and Arab support.

citation.quote: With every victory achieved by the YPG/YPJ and their allies—at Kobanî (January 2015), at Til Hemîs (February 2015), at Girê Spî (June 2015), and at Şengal und Hol (November 2015)—Arab support for the YPG grows stronger.

title: Report confirms continued attacks on Syriac churches in Turkish-occupied Nîsebîn
summary: A report from Nîsebîn by Syriac chairman Yûhanna Aktaş confirmed that attacks on Syriac churches and significant sites were continuing, with the aim of expelling the Syriac population.

citation.quote: In November 2015, a report from Nîsebîn, in Turkish-occupied Kurdistan, by the Syriac chairman Yûhanna Aktaş, confirmed that attacks on Syriac churches and other significant sites continued, with the intention of driving the Syriacs out.

title: Kurdish, Arab, and Syriac youth clear seven areas in Cizîrê canton
summary: By November 2015 in Cizîrê canton, youth from Kurdish, Arab, and Syriac communities serving in the new conscript forces had cleared seven areas of hostile presence.

citation.quote: By November 2015 in Cizîrê canton, Kurdish, Arab, and Syriac youth had cleared seven areas.

title: SDF liberates 1,362 km² in southern Hesekê
summary: Within a few days in mid-November 2015, the SDF liberated a large area in southern Hesekê including the cities of Xatuniye and Hol, and 196 villages, with Arab populations welcoming their liberators.

citation.quote: Within only a few days in mid-November, the alliance was able to liberate an area of 1,362 square kilometers in southern Hesekê, which included the cities of Xatuniye (in Arabic, Al-Khatuniyah) and Hol (in Arabic, Al-Hawl), as well as 196 villages.

title: Cizîrê economics ministry describes cooperative structure to authors
summary: A member of Cizîrê's economics ministry explained that cooperatives are fully oriented toward social needs and directly connected to communes, whose elected leadership guides cooperative management.

citation.quote: "Our cooperatives are one hundred percent oriented toward the needs of society and are directly connected to the communes," a member of Cizîrê's economics ministry told us in November 2015. "The communes elect the cooperatives' leadership. The economic commissions at all levels support them and their work through education programs."

title: YPG/YPJ, PKK, Peshmerga, and Ezidi forces jointly liberate Şengal from IS
summary: Working together, YPG/YPJ, PKK, Peshmerga, and local Ezidi forces jointly liberated the city of Şengal from IS. Afterwards, Barzanî denied that the YPG, YPJ, or PKK had participated, crediting only the Peshmerga.

citation.quote: Then in November 2015, working together, YPG/YPJ, PKK, Peshmerga, and local Ezidi forces jointly liberated the city of Şengal from IS once and for all. Afterwards, Barzanî denied that the YPG, the YPJ, or the PKK had participated, giving full credit to the Peshmerga.

title: AKP wins Turkish snap election
summary: The AKP succeeded in a so-called snap election on November 1, 2015, following its ruthless campaign against the HDP and Kurdish movement.

citation.quote: The ruthless campaign contributed to the success of the AKP in a so-called "snap election" on November 1, 2015.

title: HDP receives nearly 11 percent in Turkish elections
summary: Despite disappointing results in the November 1, 2015 Turkish elections, the pro-Kurdish and leftist HDP still received almost 11 percent of the vote, continuing to pursue diplomacy and a peaceful solution as its basic aims.

citation.quote: Despite the disappointing electoral results of November 1, 2015, the pro-Kurdish and leftist HDP still received almost 11 percent of the vote, and the movement now considers diplomacy and a peaceful solution to be its basic aims.

title: Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) founded
summary: The Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) were founded on November 11, 2015, as a multi-ethnic armed alliance in northern Syria.

citation.quote: It followed on the heels of the founding of the Syrian Defense Forces (SDF) on November 11, 2015.

title: Military operation to liberate Şengal begins
summary: A major multi-force operation launched to liberate Şengal, involving YBŞ, YJÊ, HPG, YJA Star, YPG, YPJ, and Peshmerga units — 7,500 fighters in total — successfully routing IS.

citation.quote: On the morning of November 12, 2015, a major military operation to liberate Şengal began. Participants included the resistance units of Şengal, the Yekîneyên Berxwedana Şengalê (YBŞ) and the Yekîneyên Jinên Êzîdxan (YJÊ), the Ezidi women's unit; the HPG and YJA Star (PKK forces); the YPG and YPJ from Rojava; and Peshmerga units.

title: Turkey shoots down Russian Su-24 jet over Syria
summary: The Turkish Army shot down a Russian Sukhoi-24 aircraft. One pilot, Oleg Peschkow, parachuted and was killed in the air by Alparslan Çelik, a Turkish ultranationalist from the milieu of the Grey Wolves serving with a Syrian Turkmen unit backed by Turkey.

citation.quote: On November 24, 2015, the Turkish Army shot down a Russian Suchkhoi-24 jet. One of the pilots, Oleg Peschkow, parachuted and was shot dead while in the air. The killer was Alparslan Çelik, a Turk from Elazığ who comes from the milieu of the fascistic Grey Wolves.

title: Jabhat Al-Nusra and Ahrar Al-Sham attack Ezidi village of Basufan in Afrîn canton
summary: Terror militias of Jabhat Al-Nusra and Ahrar Al-Sham attacked the Ezidi village of Basufan in Afrîn canton with heavy weapons, underscoring continued Ezidi insecurity.

citation.quote: on November 25, 2015, terror militias of Jabhat Al-Nusra and the allegedly "moderate" Ahrar Al-Sham attacked the Ezidi village of Basufan in Afrîn canton with heavy weapons.

title: Syrian Democratic Council (MDS) founded in Dêrîk
summary: The Syrian Democratic Council (Meclîsa Demokratîka Suriya, MDS) was founded in Dêrîk city in December 2015 as the political wing of the SDF, working toward Democratic Autonomy in liberated areas and a federal system.

citation.quote: In December 2015, the next relevant step was the foundation of the Syrian Democratic Council (Meclîsa Demokratîka Suriya, MDS) in Dêrîk city, as its political wing, to work for Democratic Autonomy in the liberated areas and the implementation of a federal system.

title: KDP accepts Turkish soldiers into Mosul region
summary: In December 2015, the KDP accepted a contingent of several thousand Turkish soldiers into the Mosul region.

citation.quote: It was in that context that in December 2015 the KDP accepted a contingent of several thousand Turkish soldiers into the Mosul region.

title: Syrian Democratic Council (MDS) founded
summary: The Syrian Democratic Council (MDS) was founded in December 2015 alongside the SDF, providing a political framework for multi-ethnic democratic governance in Syria.

citation.quote: The formation of the SDF in October 2015 and the Syrian Democratic Council (MDS) in December 2015 is a beacon of hope for the whole region.

title: Over 187,000 displaced Kobanî residents return home
summary: By December 2015, more than 187,000 of Kobanî's former 450,000 inhabitants had returned, with residents clearing 1.4 million tons of rubble, though reconstruction lagged due to embargo, leaving thousands in tents as winter arrived.

citation.quote: As of December 2015, more than 187,000 of the Kobanî's former 450,000 inhabitants have returned. The people have made efforts to clear the city: 1.4 million tons of rubble have been removed, with scant technical support.

title: Democratic Council of Syria established
summary: The political alliance Democratic Council of Syria was established as a complement to the SDF military alliance, two months after the SDF's founding.

citation.quote: Complementary to the SDF, the political alliance Democratic Council of Syria was established on December 10, 2015.

title: First Kobanî Health Congress issues Rojava health policy declaration
summary: On December 25, 2015, the First Kobanî Health Congress issued a declaration summarizing Rojava's health policy, emphasizing ecological society, women's leadership in health care, natural health perspectives, and opposition to capitalist commodification of medicine.

citation.quote: On December 25, 2015, the First Kobanî Health Congress issued a document summarizing Rojava's health policy. It highlighted that health care is essential "for the construction of … an ecological society"; that women are "the avant-garde of health care"; that "a natural health perspective" is essential; that health care as "commodified by capitalist modernity" has manufactured demand for dubious services and made people dependent on them.

title: Estimated 4,000 YPG/YPJ fighters killed in Rojava conflict
summary: By the summer of 2016, an estimated 4,000 YPG and YPJ fighters had been killed defending Rojava, casualties attributed in part to Western states, Gulf monarchies, and Turkey having initially armed radical Syrian opposition forces.

citation.chapter: 8.11 The Significance of the YPG and YPJ
citation.quote: As of the summer of 2016, an estimated 4,000 fighters have been killed.

title: Cases handled by Rojava peace committees and people's courts decline
summary: By early 2016, the number of cases brought before Rojava's peace committees and people's courts had declined, with interview partners across Rojava attributing the drop to the success of community-level conflict resolution and the women's movement's work against "honor" killings.

citation.quote: As of early 2016, the number of cases handled by the peace committees and people's courts has declined; reliable figures are hard to come by, but every interview partner in Rojava emphasized such a decline.

title: Justice platforms scheduled for assessment in Rojava
summary: In 2016, the justice platforms were to be assessed, allowing the people to decide whether and how to proceed with them as an experiment in democratizing the justice system.

citation.quote: Later in 2016, the justice platforms will be assessed, and the people will be able to decide whether and how to proceed with them.

title: Rojava's education transformation advances significantly
summary: By early 2016, the education transformation in Rojava was much farther along, moving slowly but surely based on widespread discussions.

citation.quote: By early 2016, the transformation was much farther along, moving slowly but surely based on widespread discussions in Rojava, so as to be well-grounded and long-lasting.

title: First health academy opens in Kobanî
summary: In early 2016, the first health academy in Rojava opened in Kobanî, following the resolution passed at the Cizîrê Health Congress in September 2015.

citation.quote: In early 2016, the first health academy opened in Kobanî.

title: Turkish Army destroys Nisêbîn water treatment facility construction
summary: Construction of a new water treatment facility in Nisêbîn was halted first by financial difficulties and then destroyed by the Turkish Army in spring 2016, leaving wastewater untreated.

citation.quote: Nisêbîn was planning to build a new water treatment facility, but construction was halted due to financial difficulties, and more recently by the Turkish Army's destruction in the spring of 2016.

title: Turkish forces shell YPG/YPJ attempting to cross Euphrates near Jarabulus
summary: When the YPG/YPJ tried to cross the Euphrates near Jarabulus in spring 2016, Turkish artillery shelled them and Turkish planes bombed them, preventing any advance toward connecting Afrîn and Kobanî.

citation.quote: In Jarabulus, an IS stronghold and a border crossing connecting IS with Turkey, residents are asking for help against IS rule, but when the YPG/YPG tried to cross the river in the spring of 2016, Turkish artillery shelled them, and Turkish planes bombed them.

title: Jihadist militias launch intensive attacks on Şêx Maqsud in Aleppo
summary: Starting in early 2016, jihadist militias including Ahrar Al-Sham and Jaish Al-Islam attacked the Kurdish neighborhood of Şêx Maqsud in Aleppo with heavy weapons, missiles, and chemical weapons.

citation.quote: Starting in early 2016, jihadist militias intensively attacked the neighborhood with heavy weapons and missiles. Ahrar Al-Sham and Jaish Al-Islam used chemical weapons.

title: Geneva talks' third attempt excludes Rojava and PYD
summary: The international powers' third round of Geneva negotiations on Syria's future took place in January and February 2016. Rojava's self-government and the PYD were specifically excluded to accommodate Turkey's anti-Kurdish position, while Ahrar Al-Sham and Jaish Al-Islam were included.

citation.quote: The negotiation process at Geneva to discuss the future of Syria, set up by the international powers, began its third attempt at negotiation in January and February 2016. Ahrar Al-Sham and Jaish Al-Islam were included as participants—in fact, Mohammed Alloush of Jaish Al-Islam is on the negotiating committee.

title: Geneva III conference convened on Syrian civil war
summary: The Geneva III conference in January 2016 again attempted to negotiate a solution to Syria's civil war. As at Geneva II, Rojava's participation was obstructed by Turkey's anti-Kurdish position requiring Kurds to join "the opposition."

citation.quote: A similar conditionality was observable in the negotiations over participation at the Geneva II conference in January 2014 and Geneva III in January 2016.

title: Letter from Ahrar Al-Sham to Jabhat Al-Nusra implicates KDP and ENKS in Aleppo offensive
summary: A discovered letter dated January 4, 2016 from Ahrar Al-Sham to Jabhat Al-Nusra, if authentic, establishes that the KDP and ENKS, with help from the AKP and Turkish intelligence, sent military units toward Aleppo.

citation.quote: A recently discovered letter from Ahrar Al-Sham to Jabhat Al-Nusra dated January 4, 2016, if authentic, establishes that the KDP and the ENKS, with help of the AKP and Turkish intelligence, sent military units toward Aleppo.

title: First school for disabled and special needs students opens in Kobanî
summary: On February 1, 2016, the Kobanî community opened its first school for disabled and special needs students, led by blind teacher Suleyman Mahmoud, with 15 students enrolled.

citation.quote: On February 1, 2016, the community opened the first school for disabled and special needs students, to great enthusiasm. With 15 students enrolled, the school will teach Kurdish and computer skills among other subjects.

title: SDF frees Al-Shaddadi, last IS city in Hesekê
summary: On February 19, 2016, the SDF liberated Al-Shaddadi, the last major city under IS control in Hesekê province.

citation.quote: On February 19, 2016, the SDF freed Al-Shaddadi, the last major city under the control of IS in Hesekê province.

title: Declaration and establishment of the Federal System of Rojava/Northern Syria
summary: In March 2016, the Federal System of Rojava/Northern Syria was declared and established, bringing the three cantons together with newly liberated areas as a potential third-way alternative to Assad's regime and chauvinist-Islamist forces.

citation.quote: Meanwhile in Syria, the declaration and establishment of the Federal System of Rojava/Northern Syria in March 2016 has the potential, as a "third way," to rupture the broad dominance of the Assad regime and the chauvinist-Islamist forces.

title: KRG closes Semalka border crossing to Rojava
summary: In March 2016, the Kurdistan Regional Government closed the Semalka border crossing entirely, barring even journalists from crossing into Rojava.

citation.quote: In March 2016, the KRG closed the Semalka border crossing altogether, even to journalists.

title: Syrian Democratic Forces become a factor in Syria-wide process
summary: The Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF), associated with the Federal System of Rojava/Northern Syria, became a factor in the Syria-wide political and military process in March 2016.

citation.quote: the Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) associated with the Federal System of Rojava/Northern Syria, became a factor in the Syrian-wide process in March 2016.

title: Federal System of Rojava/Northern Syria declared
summary: In March 2016, the Federal System of Rojava/Northern Syria was declared, introducing a new dimension for building a multi-identity, democratic Syria.

citation.quote: In January 2014, the three cantons announced the Social Contract, which says they regard themselves as part of a democratic Syria; the same is true of the Federal System of Rojava/Northern Syria, declared in March 2016.

title: Federal System of Rojava/Northern Syria declared at Rimelan assembly
summary: Thirty-one political parties and 200 delegates met for two days in Rimelan and issued a declaration establishing the Federal System in Rojava/Northern Syria (FRNS), written in Arabic. The founding meeting elected a coordinating body of 31 people and 2 co-chairs.

citation.chapter: 6.9 The Federal System of Rojava/Northern Syria (FRNS)
citation.quote: on March 17, 2016, 31 political parties and 200 delegates met for two days in Rimelan. They represented the DAAs, recently liberated areas outside the cantons, and not-yet-liberated areas (like the Shehba region between Kobanî and Afrîn), supported by the MSD. The meeting issued a declaration for a Federal System in Rojava/Northern Syria (FRNS), written in Arabic.

title: Federal System of Rojava/Northern Syria declared
summary: In response to their exclusion from the Geneva talks, the three cantons declared the Federal System of Rojava/Northern Syria on March 17, 2016, as a step toward a multi-ethnic and multi-religious alternative in Syria.

citation.quote: It was in response to their exclusion from Geneva that on March 17 they declared the Federal System of Rojava/Northern Syria [see [6.9]], as a step toward a multi-ethnic and multi-religious alternative in Syria.

title: Ba'ath regime mounts large attack on liberated areas near Qamişlo
summary: In mid-April 2016 the Ba'ath regime launched a major offensive against liberated areas, resulting in the deaths of several dozen Syrian soldiers and YPG/YPJ/Asayîş members before the regime force was defeated.

citation.quote: In mid-April 2016, the Ba'ath regime mounted a large attack that led to the deaths of several dozen Syrian soldiers and YPG/YPJ/Asayîş members. The regime force was defeated.

title: Syrian parliamentary elections held; Rojava self-government boycotts
summary: In April 2016, Syrian parliamentary elections were held. Rojava's self-government again boycotted the vote, refusing to recognize the Assad regime's authority over the cantons.

citation.quote: In June 2014 and in April 2016, when the Syrian presidential and parliamentary elections were held, regime supporters living in the neighborhoods of Qamişlo voted, but Rojava's self-government boycotted the elections on the grounds that the cantons did not recognize the regime as long as the regime didn't recognize the cantons.

title: Weapons transported over Turkish border at Kilis under intelligence observation
summary: According to the ANHA news agency, on April 14, 2016, weapons were transported over the Turkish border at Kilis under Turkish intelligence observation, with Uzbek and Turkmen fighters waiting to be brought to Azaz to reinforce Turkey's occupation zone.

citation.quote: According to the ANHA news agency, on April 14, 2016, weapons were transported over the border at Kilis, under the observation of Turkish intelligence. Uzbek and Turkmen fighters waited on the border to be brought to Azaz to strengthen Turkey's "occupation zone."

title: SDF begins operation to liberate Raqqa
summary: In May 2016, the SDF launched an operation to liberate Raqqa, aiming to free territory north of the city and cut IS supply routes, under the command of Rojda Felat.

citation.quote: In May 2016, the SDF began an operation to liberate Raqqa. The leading commander, Rojda Felat, explained that this operation's goal is to free much of the area north of Raqqa and take control of the roads connecting IS with other areas it occupies.

title: Kobanî canton limits well numbers to protect water supply
summary: The agriculture ministry of Kobanî canton decided to limit the number of wells in order to protect the groundwater supply, a measure the authors describe as wise and urge other cantons to replicate.

citation.quote: In May 2016, the agriculture ministry of Kobanî canton decided to limit the number of wells to protect the supply.

title: SDF launches 'Abu Leyla' operation to liberate Manbij
summary: At the beginning of June 2016, the SDF launched a comprehensive military operation to liberate Manbij, named 'Abu Leyla' in memory of a commander killed by IS at the start of the operation.

citation.quote: At the beginning of June 2016, the SDF began a comprehensive operation to liberate Manbij. The operation was named "Abu Leyla" in memory of a beloved commander from an Arab tribe who was killed by IS at the beginning of the operation; he had played an important role in the liberation of Kobanî.

title: SDF launches offensive on Manbij, cuts Jarabulus–Raqqa road
summary: In June 2016, the SDF severed the road between Jarabulus and Raqqa and launched a massive offensive on Manbij against the Islamic State.

citation.quote: In June 2016, the SDF cut the road between Jarabulus and Raqqa, starting a massive offensive on Manbij.

title: KDP announces Semalka border crossing will reopen after protests
summary: Following protests in South Kurdistan, the KDP announced in June 2016 that the Semalka crossing would reopen, though in practice it severely limited crossings and the transport of food supplies.

citation.quote: In June, after protests in South Kurdistan, the KDP announced it would reopen, but in reality it severely limits crossings by people and the transport of food supplies.

title: Attempted military coup in Turkey
summary: The attempted military coup of July 15, 2016, in Turkey resulted from growing conflict among reactionary forces.

citation.quote: The attempted military coup of July 15, 2016, in Turkey was the result of the growing conflict among reactionary forces.

title: Al-Nusra splits from Al-Qaeda and renames itself Jabhat Fateh Al-Sham
summary: Al-Nusra formally broke from Al-Qaeda and rebranded as Jabhat Fateh Al-Sham (Front for the Conquest of Syria), a move promoted by Turkey and Qatar since 2015 to gain international legitimacy. The United States stated the name change would not alter its assessment of the group.

citation.quote: On July 28, 2016, Al-Nusra split from Al-Qaeda and renamed itself Jabhat Fateh Al-Sham (Front for the Conquest of Syria). Turkey and Qatar had been promoting such a split since 2015, so that Al-Nusra could gain international legitimacy.

title: SDF liberates Manbij from IS
summary: On August 12, 2016, the SDF liberated Manbij, completing the Abu Leyla operation and removing IS from the strategically vital corridor between the Afrîn and Kobanî/Cizîrê cantons.

citation.quote: It liberated Manbij on August 12, 2016.
